cues.en: I've only been here in, in San Antonio for less than twenty four hours. It's getting to be about twenty four hours.
cues.zh: 我在圣安东尼奥待了还不到二十四小时。现在快满二十四小时了。

cues.en: And, I saw... I have seen actually,
cues.zh: 而且，我看到了……其实，我已经看到了，

cues.en: two parts of San Antonio.
cues.zh: 圣安东尼奥的两个部分。

cues.en: One is the well known, the famous San Antonio, the San Antonio of,
cues.zh: 一个是众所周知的、著名的圣安东尼奥，那个

cues.en: of the Riverwalk
cues.zh: Riverwalk 的圣安东尼奥。

cues.en: and the really wonderful downtown which you have,
cues.zh: 还有你们这里真正美妙的市中心，

cues.en: which is as good as any in The United States. There are no better downtowns,
cues.zh: 它和美国任何地方的一样好。没有更好的市中心了，

cues.en: than this one.
cues.zh: 比这个更好的了。

cues.en: And, it is, a downtown that is not just now beginning to get better,
cues.zh: 而且，这个市中心并不是现在才开始变好，

cues.en: but in fact, there have been, as far as I can tell, several generations of planners doing, making excellent decisions, and you can see the results.
cues.zh: 事实上，据我所知，已经有好几代规划者一直在做，做出了出色的决策，而成果有目共睹。

cues.en: That is the San Antonio which is well known to planners outside, not just the tourists, but the planners.
cues.zh: 这就是圣安东尼奥，外地规划师熟知的地方——不只是游客知道，规划师也知道。

cues.en: There is another San Antonio outside of that area,
cues.zh: 在那片区域之外，还有另一个圣安东尼奥，

cues.en: which is identical
cues.zh: 它如出一辙，

cues.en: to the mess that is occurring in most other cities. It's the pattern of suburban sprawl.
cues.zh: 和大多数其他城市正在发生的那团混乱一样。这就是郊区蔓延的模式。

cues.en: That is the San Antonio,
cues.zh: 这就是那个圣安东尼奥，

cues.en: which,
cues.zh: 它，

cues.en: no one takes you to visit
cues.zh: 没人会带你去参观，

cues.en: and,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: is unremarkable in every way. And it is in fact the pattern of growth that will make this place
cues.zh: 在各方面都平平无奇。而事实上，正是这种增长模式会让这个地方

cues.en: ultimately
cues.zh: 最终

cues.en: choke
cues.zh: 窒息，

cues.en: as surely as other cities have choked that have followed this pattern.
cues.zh: 就像其他遵循这种模式的城市一样，必然也会窒息。

cues.en: By choke, mean the inability to sustain growth.
cues.zh: 我说的“窒息”，是指无法持续增长。

cues.en: Now, I come from a city
cues.zh: 我来自一座城市

cues.en: that is an excellent laboratory. I mean, I intimately know
cues.zh: 它是个绝佳的实验室。我是说，我非常熟悉

cues.en: Miami and the history of planning in Miami and what has happened.
cues.zh: 迈阿密、迈阿密的规划史，以及那里发生过的一切。

cues.en: This is the
cues.zh: 这是

cues.en: headline that we received on Monday, 10/02/1989
cues.zh: 我们在1989年10月2日星期一收到的标题

cues.en: that announced that Miami could grow no further.
cues.zh: 它宣布迈阿密不能再继续增长。

cues.en: That this was it. There was a comprehensive planning act in, that the state of Florida promulgated that said you you could know... You
cues.zh: 事情就是这样。佛罗里达州颁布了一项综合规划法案，其中规定，你……你的

cues.en: growth would not be permitted if it were not,
cues.zh: 增长将不被允许，除非它

cues.en: concurrent with the provision of infrastructure,
cues.zh: 与基础设施的提供同步，

cues.en: which is to say roads and schools.
cues.zh: 也就是道路和学校。

cues.en: And since Miami or Dade County, like almost every other American city, no longer has the money to build the infrastructure.
cues.zh: 迈阿密或戴德县，和几乎所有其他美国城市一样，已经没钱建设基础设施了。

cues.en: It closed down growth.
cues.zh: 它阻断了增长。

cues.en: What has been happening all over areas
cues.zh: 而各地正在发生的情况

cues.en: like Dade County or the or the areas outside of Washington DC or the area around Boston and Cape Cod or around Los Angeles or around Sacramento
cues.zh: 比如戴德县，或者华盛顿特区以外的地区，或者波士顿和科德角周边，或者洛杉矶、萨克拉门托周边

cues.en: is that growth is shutting down. Developers are not welcome.
cues.zh: 就是增长正在停滞。开发商不再受欢迎了。

cues.en: Now that's a remarkable situation because throughout our history,
cues.zh: 这是个很值得注意的局面，因为纵观我们的历史，

cues.en: we have, as a society,
cues.zh: 作为一个社会，我们

cues.en: welcomed growth that has always been positive. You know, the tax base, people, jobs,
cues.zh: 一直欢迎增长，而增长一直是积极的。你知道，税基、人口、就业、

cues.en: economic well-being, all of these things come from growth. And it's actually remarkable when you get into a position where you no longer want growth, when the citizens will actually come out and say, no more.
cues.zh: 经济福祉，所有这些都来自增长。而当你走到不再想要增长的位置，当市民真的站出来说"够了"，这确实很值得注意。

cues.en: Well, that's being achieved all over The United States.
cues.zh: 嗯，这在美国各地都在实现。

cues.en: There is the idea that somehow if growth were better planned,
cues.zh: 有一种观点认为，如果增长能被更好地规划，

cues.en: it would all come out right.
cues.zh: 结果就会一切顺利。

cues.en: That is not the case because there's an awful lot of good planning
cues.zh: 但事实并非如此，因为已经有大量良好的规划

cues.en: that has been going on in the Sunbelt. For example, this is a community somewhere in the Southwest,
cues.zh: 一直在阳光地带进行。比如，这是西南部某地的一个社区，

cues.en: a so called planned community,
cues.zh: 一个所谓的规划社区，

cues.en: which you can see is, the kind of place that, planners with codes this thick have been zealously administering.
cues.zh: 你能看到，这就是那种地方——规划师们捧着这么厚的法规，一直孜孜不倦地管着。

cues.en: We have these when we have had these in Dade County and around Orlando for twenty years.
cues.zh: 我们在 Dade County 和 Orlando 周边已经有这些做法二十年了。

cues.en: But in fact,
cues.zh: 但事实上，

cues.en: growth has choked just as if there had been no planning.
cues.zh: 增长已经窒息，就好像根本没有规划一样。

cues.en: The problem is not that growth itself is bad, but that the pattern of growth, if this is the pattern of growth which is selected,
cues.zh: 问题不在于增长本身不好，而在于增长的模式——如果选中的正是这种增长模式，

cues.en: it cannot be sustained in the long term, and it will it will close down, in fact, your, your system, and it'll close down your development community.
cues.zh: 它就无法长期持续，而且事实上，它会拖垮你的系统，也会拖垮你的开发社区。

cues.en: What does this pattern consist of?
cues.zh: 这个模式由什么组成？

cues.en: The pattern is... Which I'm gonna call throughout this, this talk today, suburban sprawl,
cues.zh: 这个模式……在今天的演讲里，我会一直把它称作“郊区蔓延”，

cues.en: is an extremely
cues.zh: 它其实是一种极其

cues.en: simple organism.
cues.zh: 简单的组织形态。

cues.en: It
cues.zh: 它

cues.en: consists of just four components.
cues.zh: 只由四个组成部分构成。

cues.en: It consists of housing clusters,
cues.zh: 它由住宅组团构成，

cues.en: like this one.
cues.zh: 就像这个。

cues.en: It consists of shopping centers,
cues.zh: 它由购物中心构成，

cues.en: like this one. Of office parks,
cues.zh: 就像这个。还有办公园区，

cues.en: like this one.
cues.zh: 就像这个。

cues.en: And it consists of the meeting places that we have, our schools
cues.zh: 它还由我们的公共聚集场所构成，比如学校

cues.en: and post offices and city halls and so forth, like this one, which are usually assembled at the at the end of a Collector Street in something called a pod.
cues.zh: 和邮局、市政厅等等，就像这个，它们通常被集中布置在集散街道的尽头，形成所谓的“组团”。

cues.en: To
cues.zh: 为了

cues.en: remind you of two examples in San Antonio,
cues.zh: 提醒你圣安东尼奥的两个例子，

cues.en: the
cues.zh: 那个

cues.en: the, I believe it's called the University of Texas at San Antonio,
cues.zh: 那个，我记得叫德克萨斯大学圣安东尼奥分校，

cues.en: is in fact in one of these pod conditions.
cues.zh: 实际上就处于这些 pod 状况之一。

cues.en: And there is also that medical complex, in that,
cues.zh: 还有那个医疗综合体，在那个，

cues.en: north, northwestern direction. What's it called?
cues.zh: 北边、西北方向。它叫什么来着？

cues.en: That
cues.zh: 那个

cues.en: one. That's... That medical center is also one of these pod situations.
cues.zh: 那个。那是……那个医疗中心也是这些 pod 情形之一。

cues.en: And I am told by the city traffic engineer that that is where traffic is worse,
cues.zh: 而且城市交通工程师告诉我，那里交通更糟，

cues.en: in fact. Well, that's typical of the situation.
cues.zh: 事实上。嗯，这种情况很典型。

cues.en: When you when you put elements like these at at, single use elements at the ends of Collector Streets,
cues.zh: 当你把这类元素——单一用途元素——放在集散道路尽头时，

cues.en: ultimately, what chokes growth is is is traffic. It cannot be sustained.
cues.zh: 最终，扼杀增长的是交通。这种模式无法持续。

cues.en: Now the interesting thing about these four elements
cues.zh: 这四种元素有意思的地方在于

cues.en: is that all four are necessary for life. I mean, what we're talking about here is places where people live, where places where people shop, places where people work, and places where people gather.
cues.zh: 它们对生活都不可或缺。我的意思是，我们谈的是人们居住的地方、购物的地方、工作的地方和聚集的地方。

cues.en: It is the humans need this for their habitat.
cues.zh: 这是人类需要的栖息地。

cues.en: How is it that these humans that need these places are actually get to the position that they're against growth? You know, how do you arrive at that condition?
cues.zh: 这些需要这些地方的人，怎么反而会站到反对增长的位置上？你是怎么走到那种境地的？

cues.en: Well, we've analyzed it.
cues.zh: 这个我们分析过。

cues.en: And what we found by... This by speaking to people, not a, you know, not a big study. We're not the Gallup organization.
cues.zh: 我们的发现来自……跟人交谈，不是什么大型研究。我们可不是盖洛普那种机构。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: when you when you speak to people who live in the suburbs, you find two contradictory,
cues.zh: 当你跟住在郊区的人聊，你会发现两种相互矛盾的、

cues.en: I think, opinions.
cues.zh: 我认为，观点。

cues.en: One is that they like where they live.
cues.zh: 有人喜欢自己住的地方。

cues.en: They like their house and they like their lot, but they don't want any more of it.
cues.zh: 他们喜欢自己的房子和地块，但并不想要更多。

cues.en: Now when you delve further,
cues.zh: 再深入探究一下，

cues.en: what you find is that they actually
cues.zh: 你会发现他们实际上

cues.en: like their private realm.
cues.zh: 喜欢自己的私人空间。

cues.en: They very much like what the developers have provided them in terms of interiors,
cues.zh: 他们非常喜欢开发商提供的室内配置，

cues.en: bathrooms,
cues.zh: 浴室、

cues.en: square footage, heating, air conditioning, washing machines, appliances, convenience of parking,
cues.zh: 面积、供暖、空调、洗衣机、家电、停车的便利，

cues.en: and so forth. They also like their country clubs. They like their golf courses.
cues.zh: 等等。他们也喜欢自己的乡村俱乐部。他们喜欢高尔夫球场。

cues.en: What they don't like is the public realm.
cues.zh: 他们不喜欢的是公共空间。

cues.en: As soon as they step out of their front yard,
cues.zh: 他们一走出前院，

cues.en: they enter
cues.zh: 就会进入

cues.en: a a situation which is essentially harsh,
cues.zh: 一种本质上严酷、

cues.en: stressful,
cues.zh: 充满压力、

cues.en: and ugly. The public realm is
cues.zh: 又丑陋的处境。公共空间

cues.en: tough to be in in the suburbs.
cues.zh: 在郊区很难待下去。

cues.en: This is as opposed to the public realm that you have here in Downtown San Antonio. The great success
cues.zh: 这与你们圣安东尼奥市中心的公共空间形成对比。最大的成功

cues.en: of Downtown San Antonio is not the specific hotels, you know, the Marriott or the or this or that shopping because you can find that in the suburbs. The great success
cues.zh: 并不在于圣安东尼奥市中心的具体酒店，你知道，Marriott，或者这个那个商场，因为郊区也能找到这些。最大的成功

cues.en: is that it's a great public realm. The streets and the squares are beautifully designed for people.
cues.zh: 而在于它是一个很棒的公共空间。街道和广场都为人们做了精美的设计。

cues.en: That is completely the opposite of what's happening in the suburb. The public realm is is a rough place to be. That is what they don't want.
cues.zh: 这跟郊区的情况完全相反。公共空间是个粗糙、不好待的地方。这正是他们不想要的。

cues.en: Now what we're proposing as a pattern here is is is to is to continue... Is to build in the suburbs
cues.zh: 现在我们提出的一种模式，就是继续……就是在郊区建设

cues.en: with a public realm which is of that same quality. A public realm which is as good to be in as the one that you have downtown. And I'm gonna and I'm gonna specify exactly how this this is done. And at this point, this presentation gets quite technical.
cues.zh: 一个具有同样品质的公共空间。一个待起来和在市中心一样好的公共空间。接下来我会具体说明这到底是怎么做的。讲到这里，这个演示会变得相当技术性。

cues.en: These are two places in Virginia, not too far from each other. This one's called Virginia Beach. That one is called Alexandria.
cues.zh: 这是弗吉尼亚州的两个地方，彼此离得不远。这个叫 Virginia Beach，那个叫 Alexandria。

cues.en: They're both flattering photographs,
cues.zh: 这两张照片都拍得很上镜，

cues.en: believe it or not.
cues.zh: 信不信由你。

cues.en: This one comes from the promotional brochure of the city of Virginia Beach. When you go there, they give you this. They say, becoming a showcase, Virginia Beach Boulevard Phase 1 celebrated its opening.
cues.zh: 这张来自 Virginia Beach 市的宣传册。你去那里，他们就会给你这个。他们说，Virginia Beach Boulevard 一期成了展示样板，并庆祝了开通。

cues.en: Now what's happening here is that this is what the plan of Virginia Beach has in mind for this city. This is what they have in mind. You laugh, but this is very similar to what your suburban code has in mind for the surroundings of Downtown San Antonio. What you see here is not substantially different than what you see there. This is what the code has in mind. Now what is this code what is this code concerned about?
cues.zh: 现在这里发生的是，这就是 Virginia Beach 的规划为这座城市设想的模样。这就是他们的设想。你笑了，但这和你们郊区的规范为圣安东尼奥市中心周边所设想的非常相似。你在这里看到的，和你在那边看到的并没有本质不同。这就是规范所设想的。那么这个规范，这个规范关心的是什么？

cues.en: Well, perfectly objectively,
cues.zh: 嗯，完全客观地说，

cues.en: the most important thing that this code is concerned about is that cars should be happy.
cues.zh: 这段代码最关心的事情，就是汽车应该开心。

cues.en: You see? These are happy cars
cues.zh: 看到了吗？这些都是开心的汽车

cues.en: because they never have to stack up more than six at a time. They
cues.zh: 因为它们一次最多只需排到六辆。它们

cues.en: make nice easy turns. They don't strain their little steering wheels doing that,
cues.zh: 转弯轻松顺畅。这样做时，它们的小方向盘也不会吃不消，

cues.en: and they can park even on the worst retail day of the year. That parking
cues.zh: 而且即使在一年中零售最繁忙的那天也能停车。那个停车

cues.en: lot is rated for the Saturday before Christmas. Now the fact
cues.zh: 场是按圣诞节前的周六来设计的。现在，事实

cues.en: the fact that, you know, for the rest of the year, it is from one third to two thirds empty, that's irrelevant. It's always maximized, the maximum efficiency.
cues.zh: 事实是，你知道，在一年中其余时间，它有三分之一到三分之二是空的，这无关紧要。它总是被最大化，达到最高效率。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: the other thing that this code is terribly concerned about is that the uses not be mixed. It's very, very important
cues.zh: 这套法规还非常在意另一点：用途不能混杂。这一点非常非常重要

cues.en: to the planners of Virginia Beach that everything here be retail.
cues.zh: 对 Virginia Beach 的规划者来说，这里的一切都必须是零售用途。

cues.en: This is a shopping center or or a retail area.
cues.zh: 这里是购物中心，或者说是零售区。

cues.en: The offices are... Where you work are elsewhere. The residential is elsewhere. Everything that you see here, whether it's big or small, this is a very big mall here, and then there's a tiny little bank and a couple of medium sized,
cues.zh: 办公室……你工作的地方在别处。住宅区在别处。你在这里看到的一切，无论大小——这里有个很大的商场，还有一家很小的银行，以及几家中等规模的

cues.en: eating places.
cues.zh: 餐饮店。

cues.en: Everything here is of a single use, which is
cues.zh: 这里的一切都是单一用途，也就是

cues.en: retail.
cues.zh: 零售。

cues.en: Now, let's talk about this as an environment.
cues.zh: 现在，我们把它当作一种环境来谈。

cues.en: It's not that these planners don't care about people. Obviously, there's a sidewalk code somewhere here.
cues.zh: 并不是这些规划者不关心人。显然，这里某处有人行道规范。

cues.en: But you know perfectly well from experience that only indigence are to be found in places like that. If you actually see somebody halfway decently dressed,
cues.zh: 但经验告诉你，那种地方只会看到穷人。如果你真看到穿着还算体面的人，

cues.en: walking in the sidewalk, you stop to help them out because obviously some problem.
cues.zh: 走在人行道上，你会停下来帮他们，因为显然出了什么问题。

cues.en: It is actually...
cues.zh: 其实……

cues.en: That kind of environment is... It is embarrassing
cues.zh: 那种环境……挺让人难堪的

cues.en: to be seen walking, admit it, in a place like this. Only the underclass is found as a pedestrian here.
cues.zh: 承认吧，在这种地方被人看到在走路，是件丢人的事。在这里，只有底层人才会步行。

cues.en: There's a sidewalk, but it's a completely unworkable sidewalk.
cues.zh: 这里有人行道，但完全是没法用的人行道。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: obviously, here, there's also a landscape ordinance
cues.zh: 显然，这里还有景观条例

cues.en: and even a tree preservation ordinance.
cues.zh: 甚至还有树木保护条例。

cues.en: And it's important to say this,
cues.zh: 这一点很重要，

cues.en: and the signs don't look too bad. You don't see too many signs. It's important to say this because,
cues.zh: 而且这些标识看起来还不算太糟。你不会看到太多标识。说这一点很重要，因为，

cues.en: after one generation of this kind of planner... Of planning, most planners have said... Have looked at it and said, this
cues.zh: 经过一代这种规划者……这种规划之后，大多数规划者都说……都看过之后说，这

cues.en: this doesn't look so good. Let's pass additional ordinances,
cues.zh: 这看起来不太好。我们再加一些条例吧，

cues.en: for example, that require trees in the parking lot and require berms.
cues.zh: 比如，要求停车场里种树，还要求设置土堤。

cues.en: But that isn't the issue at all. The problem with this is not that it is ugly. The problem is that it doesn't work. It can't be sustained.
cues.zh: 但这根本不是问题所在。问题不在于它难看，而在于它行不通。它无法持续。

cues.en: And I'm gonna show you some beautiful suburban sprawl later on. So don't be confused
cues.zh: 稍后我会给你们看一些漂亮的郊区蔓延。所以别搞混了

cues.en: by sign ordinances,
cues.zh: 被标牌法规、

cues.en: burns, landscape. Those are fine, but they're only cosmetic. They really don't get at the heart of the problem.

And besides, that twenty minutes turns into forty minutes and then turns into an hour and then into an hour and a half commute.
cues.zh: 我就会买那栋房子，因为浴室上方有天窗，或者因为，你知道，每平方英尺便宜两美元之类的，而不是把“那二十分钟是我人生的一大部分”考虑进去。而且，那二十分钟会变成四十分钟，再变成一小时，然后变成一小时半的通勤。

cues.zh: 当出现阻力时

cues.zh: 在交通中，人们开始……人们会把额外的

cues.en: information,
cues.zh: 信息考虑进去，

cues.zh: 我离上班地点还有多远？这最终就是解决方案，至少能稳定交通问题。

cues.en: Now take the alternate system here. This is Old Town Alexandria.
cues.zh: 现在看看这里另一套系统。这里是亚历山德里亚老城。

cues.en: It is, laid out... It was laid out by George Washington's father.
cues.zh: 它的布局……是由乔治·华盛顿的父亲规划的。

cues.en: And George Washington was active here, administering the code and so forth.
cues.zh: 乔治·华盛顿也曾活跃于此，负责执行法规等等。

cues.en: And the curious thing about this is that whenever I show it,
cues.zh: 有趣的是，每次我展示它，

cues.en: people think that it is a form of Williamsburg.
cues.zh: 人们都以为这是某种威廉斯堡。

cues.en: That somehow to live in a place like that, you need to wear costumes or be government subsidized or put up with incredible inconvenience or something or other. You know, have outhouses instead of toilets.
cues.zh: 好像要住在那样一个地方，你就得穿奇装异服，或者靠政府补贴，或者忍受极大的不便之类的。你知道，用旱厕而不是抽水马桶。

cues.en: But in fact,
cues.zh: 但事实上，

cues.en: in fact, these are very real people living, working, and shopping here, people with kids and jobs and everything.
cues.zh: 事实上，这些都是非常真实的人，在这里生活、工作、购物，他们有孩子、有工作，什么都有。

cues.en: Let me describe how different this is from this because it's backwards in almost every way.
cues.zh: 我来描述一下这个和这个有多不同，因为它几乎方方面面都是反着来的。

cues.en: If you look at this area here,
cues.zh: 如果你看这片区域，

cues.en: all the buildings here, what they have in common is that they're small.
cues.zh: 这里所有建筑的共同点是，它们都很小。

cues.en: What they don't have in common is that they're a single use.
cues.zh: 它们的共同点并不包括单一用途。

cues.en: See, over here, you have houses.
cues.zh: 看，这边有住宅。

cues.en: You have boarding houses. You have bed and breakfast inns. You have corner stores.
cues.zh: 有寄宿公寓。有民宿旅馆。有街角小店。

cues.en: You have
cues.zh: 这里有

cues.en: medical practitioners,
cues.zh: 执业医生，

cues.en: you have architects
cues.zh: 有建筑师

cues.en: and lawyers in operation,
cues.zh: 还有执业律师，

cues.en: but they're... You even have churches.
cues.zh: 但它们……你甚至还有教堂。

cues.en: What they have in common is that the buildings are all small. Therefore, they are compatible.
cues.zh: 它们的共同点是这些建筑都很小。因此，它们是兼容的。

cues.en: This is completely different from the kind of coding that occurs here in which the buildings can be large or small, but they're a single use.
cues.zh: 这与这里进行的编码完全不同：在这里，建筑可大可小，但都是单一用途。

cues.en: Over in this area,
cues.zh: 在这片区域，

cues.en: there are buildings that are medium sized
cues.zh: 有一些中等大小的建筑

cues.en: and then buildings that are very large.
cues.zh: 还有一些非常大的建筑。

cues.en: You see, it's small buildings with small buildings, large buildings with large buildings. All
cues.zh: 你看，小建筑配小建筑，大建筑配大建筑。所有

cues.en: of these things are compatible as long as the use... As long as the sizes are similar.
cues.zh: 这些东西只要用途……只要大小相近，就是兼容的。

cues.en: So do you see the codes are written completely differently. The code that makes this place
cues.zh: 所以你看，这些规范写得完全不同。塑造这个地方的规范

cues.en: worries about how building or is concerned about how buildings behave in terms of physical size and disposition relative to the street. As long as the buildings are pulled up to the street and they're not over a certain size, they're compatible
cues.zh: 关心建筑在物理尺寸和相对街道的布置上如何表现。只要建筑紧贴街道，且不超过一定尺寸，它们就是协调的

cues.en: as opposed to this that cares very little about that.
cues.zh: 而与之相对的这套规范，几乎不关心这些。

cues.en: Well, that's the private realm. That's how the private realm works here. Now, public realm is also different.
cues.zh: 嗯，那是私人领域。这里的私人领域就是这么运作的。而公共领域也不一样。

cues.en: This... These streets here are all small and they're all complex.
cues.zh: 这里的街道都很小，而且都很复杂。

cues.en: Traffic flows slowly in them.
cues.zh: 车流在其中移动缓慢。

cues.en: This street is a very simple street. It's really a highway. It's it's a very simple street. Only one thing happens here. The only thing that happens here is that cars flow.
cues.zh: 这条街非常简单。它其实是一条公路。它就是一条非常简单的街道。这里只发生一件事：只有车流。

cues.en: Pedestrians don't. Trees don't exist. Buildings don't align the street. It's only for cars. The public realm is only for cars in this model. Here, the public realm contains not only cars that move, but cars that park,
cues.zh: 没有行人。没有树木。建筑也不沿街排列。它只服务于汽车。在这个模型里，公共空间只属于汽车。而在这里，公共空间不仅有行驶的汽车，还有停放的汽车，

cues.en: trees on the sidewalks,
cues.zh: 人行道上的树木，

cues.en: and buildings.
cues.zh: 以及建筑。

cues.en: It's a public realm, which is, because it's complex, is friendly to both cars and pedestrians.
cues.zh: 这是一个公共空间，由于它很复杂，所以对汽车和行人都很友好。

cues.en: How is this achieved?
cues.zh: 这是怎么实现的？

cues.en: It's achieved because it's a network of streets. You see? There are many, many different ways of getting from anywhere to anywhere else.
cues.zh: 这是通过街道网络实现的。你看，从任何地方到任何其他地方都有很多很多不同的路线。

cues.en: As a result of that, no one street has to be large.
cues.zh: 因此，没有哪一条街道必须很宽。

cues.en: This system, which is a system of collector streets, has very few streets that are active because the pods feed into collectors and the collectors feed on the highways. So all of these have to be very large because very few streets are actually through streets.
cues.zh: 这个系统是集散街道系统，活跃的街道很少，因为 pod 汇入集散路，集散路再汇入高速公路。所以这些道路都必须很大，因为真正贯通的道路很少。

cues.en: That's how you can get an entirely different... That's how you can get the sort of the miraculous feel of traffic flowing slowly and being friendly to pedestrians because there are many, many different ways,
cues.zh: 这样你就能得到一种完全不同的……这样你就能获得那种奇妙的感觉：车流缓慢通行，对行人友好，因为有很多很多不同的方式，

cues.zh: 像这样的零售设施，位于街区中间，它们不但不被视为碍眼之物，反而被当作大家最喜欢的聚会场所。它是社交中心。这是一家律……这是一间律师办公室，如你所见，它与两侧的住宅完全协调。现在我可以完整描述这一点。我也可以给你看一些协调的公寓楼，

cues.en: all sorts of buildings. And you've all seen them. You know what this is like, but it demonstrates
cues.zh: 各种各样的建筑。你们都见过，也知道那是什么样子，但它说明了

cues.zh: 现在，这是两个城镇中心的航拍照片，一个是旧模式，一个是新模式。这……这些其实是零售组成部分，

cues.zh: 也就是城镇中心的零售部分。

cues.zh: 这就是 Urban Land Institute 所说的邻里中心。

cues.zh: 这是

cues.zh: 一系列经过精确描述的店铺

cues.en: which contains such things as the bank,
cues.zh: 其中包括银行、

cues.zh: 问题本身不在于这个，因为这其实是这些人的社区中心。

cues.zh: 问题在于规划者，

cues.en: having inherited this mania for separating things, and this being a very advanced code that we have here in Miami, not only separates the uses,
cues.zh: 继承了这种把东西分开的狂热，而迈阿密这里又有非常先进的规范，不仅把用途分隔开，

cues.zh: 还非要确保你没法从一处走到另一处，甚至额外要求加一道墙和一条沟，

cues.zh: 因此，甚至连那些……步行一分钟……范围内的房子，也变……变……变成，

cues.en: automobile
cues.zh: 汽车

cues.zh: 通勤……的情形。这里的每个人

cues.zh: 都得钻进车里，开到 Collector Street，占用集散道的容量，再开回这里，停在离出发点一分钟路程的地方。

cues.zh: 那么，这有必要吗？这种分隔有必要吗？

cues.en: It is absolutely
cues.zh: 这绝对

cues.en: not necessary.
cues.zh: 没有必要。

cues.zh: 这源于工业革命带来的这种狂热

cues.zh: 把一切与其余一切隔开

cues.zh: 而这一切都没必要

cues.zh: 因为

cues.zh: 美国工业现在很少造成污染。

cues.en: Rarely is obnoxious.

cues.zh: 令人惊讶的是

cues.zh: 想象一下，有这么一整段连续的停车场空档。我是说，就算在你自己的市中心，有这些空档也已经够糟了，你知道，介于

cues.zh: 临街面与下一个临街面之间。有时你仍然会看到停车场。

cues.zh: 让行人能看进去的东西。现在这位建筑师也没办法，因为他受两个限制。一是建筑有退线要求，二是要求的停车位数量非常高，所以，所以除了把停车场放在前面，别无他法。

cues.en: In Princeton, New Jersey,
cues.zh: 在新泽西州的普林斯顿，

cues.en: what you find is office buildings, you know, with real people there working, real lawyers,
cues.zh: 你会发现的是办公楼，你知道，里面有真人上班，真正的律师，

cues.en: you know, real architects, real professionals working there, real insurance companies. But instead of having nothing to do at lunchtime,
cues.zh: 你知道，真正的建筑师、真正在那儿工作的专业人士、真正的保险公司。但午休时不会无事可做，

cues.en: which is a very low quality of life that you get in these suburban parks, you either have a company cafeteria or you have to get in the car and waste a lot of a lot of your time getting to an interesting place, These people come right down, and they have a huge choice of restaurants and shops, etcetera, etcetera. The parking, of course, is in the back.
cues.zh: 而在郊区园区，那种生活品质非常低：你要么有公司食堂，要么就得上车，花大把时间才能到一个有意思的地方。这些人直接下楼，就有大量餐厅和商店等等等等。停车场当然在后面。

cues.zh: 停车位设在后方的原因是，办公楼

cues.zh: 零售需要一些前方停车位，但办公楼完全不需要前方停车位，

cues.zh: 住宅情况比以往更加微妙。这里是棕榈滩县，有很多景观和湖泊，很容易看出郊区的问题未必是它们丑陋。棕榈滩县很美，到处都是景观和高尔夫球场。问题在于它运转不起来，而且是以一种非常隐蔽的方式在社会层面出问题。

cues.zh: 你看，这种按组团规划的系统

cues.zh: 还附带着

cues.en: a a segregation
cues.zh: 一种隔离

cues.zh: 住在这个组团里的人，每户都付了超过35万美元

cues.zh: 买下自己的房子。

cues.zh: 住在这个组团里的人，每户付了大约25万

cues.zh: 或更少买下自己的房子；而住在这个组团里的人——这里是四拼住宅——

cues.zh: 每户付了10万美元买下自己的房子。

cues.zh: 我们的郊区所发生的是，出于营销原因，而我认为这些原因完全是人为制造的，

cues.en: this this element of snobbism,
cues.zh: 这种这种势利心态，

cues.en: which is which is push, which is if you live in here, you're better than everyone else that lives outside, And if you live here, you're better than everyone else. And it sort of pecks on... And there's a pecking order all the way down.
cues.zh: 也就是攀比，也就是：如果你住这里，你就比住在外面的所有人都强；如果你住这里，你就比所有人都强。它就像层层啄食……而且一路下去都有等级次序。

cues.zh: 房子，就在这块空地上，这个业主协会肯定会大动肝火

cues.zh: 因为房价正在上涨。现在的情况是，人们对任何收入跟自己不完全一样的人都有极大的恐惧。我们说的不是把无家可归的人带进来，你懂的，从……从……从……从……从棕榈滩市中心。

cues.en: It's someone who has a $250,000
cues.zh: 而是某个有25万美元、

cues.en: to buy a house not being permitted to build there.
cues.zh: 想买房却不被允许在那里建房的人。

cues.en: That is completely insidious.
cues.zh: 这太阴险了。

cues.zh: 数量……那种政治碎片化

cues.en: that is taking place in the suburbs, the dislike and suspicion that people have for each other is making it virtually impossible to go... Govern intelligently.
cues.zh: 正在郊区发生，人们彼此之间的厌恶和猜疑，让明智治理几乎无法进行。

cues.en: And that's being built into this system, and it's completely unnecessary.
cues.zh: 而这正被嵌入这个系统，而且完全没有必要。

cues.en: Look at the old system.
cues.zh: 看看旧系统。

cues.en: The... Basically, the American system. This is Georgetown.
cues.zh: 那个……基本上就是美国体系。这里是乔治敦。

cues.en: On this street, you have apartment buildings on both sides of the street,
cues.zh: 在这条街上，街道两边都是公寓楼，

cues.en: which is to say quite affordable housing.
cues.zh: 也就是说，相当可负担的住房。

cues.en: Over on this street, you have townhouses facing each other, which is to say relatively more more expensive housing.
cues.zh: 在这条街上，是彼此相对的联排住宅，也就是相对更贵一些的住房。

cues.en: Then on this street, you have big houses, which is to say quite expensive housing.
cues.zh: 然后在这条街上，是大房子，也就是相当昂贵的住房。

cues.en: And finally, here on this estate, probably one of the great famous fortunes of America,
cues.zh: 最后，在这片宅邸区，大概住着美国最显赫的豪门之一，

cues.en: living in splendid... In, you know, in splendid quarters,
cues.zh: 住在富丽堂皇的……你知道，住在富丽堂皇的居所里，

cues.en: all within a very, very short
cues.zh: 这一切都位于非常非常近的

cues.en: distance
cues.zh: 距离之内

cues.en: from each other and all sharing the same public realm.
cues.zh: 彼此相距不远，而且共享同一片公共空间。

cues.en: This is the way we used to do it. Now what's interesting or rather important about mixed use planning
cues.zh: 这是我们过去的做法。现在，混合用途规划有意思、或者说重要的一点是

cues.en: is that it is not just important to have workplaces and shopping places and living places.
cues.zh: 不仅要有工作场所、购物场所和居住场所。

cues.en: It is equally important to have a range of incomes living together.
cues.zh: 同样重要的是，不同收入水平的人要住在一起。

cues.en: Because if you don't, you have to begin importing people of different incomes to work for each other. A typical situation in Palm Beach County, Palm Beach County has to send buses to Broward County to pick up workers to come cook hamburgers and mow the lawn.
cues.zh: 因为如果不这样，你就得开始引入不同收入的人，让他们互相服务。棕榈滩县的典型情况是，棕榈滩县得派巴士到布劳沃德县接工人来做汉堡、修剪草坪。

cues.en: You know, that kind of thing is going on. It's also going on in Cape Cod.
cues.zh: 你知道，这类事正在发生。在科德角也一样。

cues.en: In this system, there's the theoretical possibility
cues.zh: 在这个系统里，理论上有可能

cues.en: that that the person who mows this lawn can live within walking distance in one of these apartments.
cues.zh: 给这片草坪割草的人，能住在步行可达的这些公寓中的一套里。

cues.en: And there's another thing that's important.
cues.zh: 还有另一件重要的事。

cues.en: It isn't just important
cues.zh: 重要的不只是

cues.en: to have
cues.zh: 让

cues.en: the the the lower economic classes integrated into the upper. It is equally important to have extremely
cues.zh: 较低经济阶层融入较高阶层。同样重要的是，让极度

cues.en: wealthy people distributed
cues.zh: 富有的人分布

cues.en: among the neighborhoods and villages.
cues.zh: 在各个社区和村庄中。

cues.en: That can be seen all over the Midwest and all over the North... The Northwest. There are two types of small towns in America,
cues.zh: 这在中西部和整个北部……西北部到处都能看到。美国的小镇分两类，

cues.en: those that have one wealthy family and those that don't.
cues.zh: 一类有富裕家族，另一类没有。

cues.en: The ones who don't have that wealthy family have no culture. They're just dead ends.
cues.zh: 没有富裕家族的那些镇没有文化。它们就是死胡同。

cues.en: Those towns that have the good fortune of having had one
cues.zh: 那些有幸曾拥有过一位

cues.en: tycoon,
cues.zh: 大亨，

cues.en: one factory owner has,
cues.zh: 一位工厂主，

cues.en: those are the ones that have the beautiful parks and the museums and the and the cultural activities.
cues.zh: 这些镇才有美丽的公园、博物馆，以及各种文化活动。

cues.en: It is necessary when you have... To have a full society
cues.zh: 要有一个完整的社会，这一点是必要的。

cues.en: with, with cultural with a cultural component that there be people of wealth and leisure
cues.zh: 还要有文化成分，也就是要有既有财富又有闲暇的人

cues.en: integrated into the rest of society. Because everyone else is working too hard and doesn't have enough money to actually pursue culture. Only the very wealthy can. So it's important to build all of these things together.
cues.zh: 融入社会其他部分。因为其他人都太辛苦工作，钱也不够，没法真正追求文化。只有非常富有的人才能做到。所以把这些东西一起建设起来很重要。

cues.en: In Europe, in any city, not... It's not only in The United States
cues.zh: 在欧洲，任何城市，不……这不只在美国

cues.en: that you find that this is the this is the traditional pattern. In Europe, the great dukes,
cues.zh: 你会发现这是……这是传统模式。在欧洲，大公爵、

cues.en: the popes, and so forth, any European city that you see has the palaces next to very humble artisans' dwellings.
cues.zh: 教皇等等；你看到的任何欧洲城市，宫殿都紧挨着非常简陋的工匠住宅。

cues.en: All societies have been able to integrate by income.
cues.zh: 所有社会都能按收入融合。

cues.en: They have not been able to integrate foreigners
cues.zh: 他们却没能融合外国人

cues.en: necessarily.
cues.zh: 这并非必然。

cues.en: There are Turkish quarters and there are Jewish quarters in Europe. But by income, yes, because it is necessary and intelligent,
cues.zh: 欧洲有土耳其人聚居区，也有犹太人聚居区。但按收入，是的，因为按收入融合是必要且明智的，

cues.en: in fact, to integrate by income. It is only now that we're inventing this ridiculous system, an unnecessary system of integration.
cues.zh: 事实上，就是要按收入融合。直到现在，我们才发明出这套荒唐的制度，一套不必要的融合制度。

cues.en: And what does the... What do these residential neighborhoods look like from... Or a neighborhood is to flatter them. What do these residential components look like from the ground?
cues.zh: 那么……这些居住街区从……或者说，叫它们“街区”都算抬举了。这些住宅群从地面上看是什么样？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: this
cues.zh: 这个

cues.en: is the fast food version of the American dream, what we call the Mecca Mansion.
cues.zh: 是美国梦的快餐版，我们称之为 Mecca Mansion。

cues.en: What is what is problematic
cues.zh: 它的问题在哪

cues.en: about it is not that there is the house
cues.zh: 不在于这里有这栋房子

cues.en: and the lot because that's fine. That's the American dream. The problem is that it's a cartoon of the American dream because all you get is the illusion of privacy and the illusion of individuality.
cues.zh: 和这块地，因为那没问题。那就是美国梦。问题在于它是对美国梦的卡通化模仿，因为你得到的只是隐私的幻觉和个体性的幻觉。

cues.en: If this were assembled into a community,
cues.zh: 如果把它组装成一个社区，

cues.en: you would get both. You would get your privacy,
cues.zh: 你就能两者兼得。你会得到你的隐私、

cues.en: your individuality,
cues.zh: 你的个体性，

cues.en: but you would always get the community. See, what these give you, they only give you privacy. They don't give you community.
cues.zh: 但你总能得到社区。你看，这些东西给你的，只有隐私。它们给不了你社区。

cues.en: What we're proposing is that these single family houses and their lots be assembled into neighborhoods,
cues.zh: 我们提议的是，把这些独栋住宅及其地块整合成社区，

cues.en: that this be enriched and become a special place. What we found according to marketing, marketing studies is that people welcome both sides.
cues.zh: 让它得到丰富，成为一个特别的地方。根据营销和营销研究，我们发现人们两方面都欢迎。

cues.en: In fact, currently,
cues.zh: 事实上，目前，

cues.en: in in marketing studies, are two words that are exceptionally important to people. One is security, of course. The other one is community. They're neck and neck with each other in importance.
cues.zh: 在营销研究中，有两个词对人们格外重要。一个是安全，当然。另一个是社区。它们在重要性上不相上下。

cues.en: There's another very interesting study completed by Gallup last year,
cues.zh: 盖洛普去年完成了一项非常有趣的研究，

cues.en: which, analyzed,
cues.zh: 该研究分析了

cues.en: people in metropolitan regions, and they asked them where they would prefer to live.
cues.zh: 大都市地区的人们，并询问他们更愿意住在哪里。

cues.en: And what they responded is that 36%
cues.zh: 结果显示，36%

cues.en: wanted to live in small towns.
cues.zh: 的人想住在小城镇。

cues.en: Only 25%
cues.zh: 只有25%

cues.en: wanted to live in suburbs.
cues.zh: 的人想住在郊区。

cues.en: So it's not what people think. You see, developers and and the ULI and these people think that everyone wants to live in suburbs.
cues.zh: 所以这和人们想的不一样。你看，开发商、ULI这些人以为大家都想住郊区。

cues.en: That's not true. They want their single family houses, but they prefer to live in towns, not just suburbs.
cues.zh: 并非如此。他们想要自己的单户住宅，但他们更愿意住在城镇，而不仅仅是郊区。

cues.en: Who's providing suburb... Who's providing towns? No one. All the developers are like lemmings providing exactly the same product. You know, the pod community with the golf course attached. No wonder it is so drastically overbuilt.
cues.zh: 谁在造郊区……谁在造城镇？没人。所有开发商都像旅鼠一样，做出一模一样的产品。就是那种自带高尔夫球场的封闭式小区。难怪会严重过剩。

cues.en: Very few people are providing towns. The developers that come to us, in fact, are asking for towns because they see it as an enormous
cues.zh: 很少有人在做城镇。事实上，来找我们的开发商都在要城镇，因为他们觉得这是一个巨大的

cues.en: unmet marketing niche.
cues.zh: 尚未被满足的市场空白。

cues.en: Now, how do you provide affordable housing?
cues.zh: 那么，怎么提供可负担住房呢？

cues.en: Traditional towns give you different,
cues.zh: 传统城镇会给你不同的，

cues.en: different strategies.
cues.zh: 不同的策略。

cues.en: Two are very simple.
cues.zh: 其中两个很简单。

cues.en: One of them is do not permit people to build retail unless there is, in some measure,
cues.zh: 其中一个就是，不允许人们建零售设施，除非在某种程度上，

cues.en: housing
cues.zh: 住房

cues.en: attached to it. Because you see people,
cues.zh: 与之相连。因为你看，人们，

cues.en: merchants don't live above the store necessarily because they're they're doing too well-to-do that. Anybody who owns a liquor store can afford the American dream of the single family house. The people who live near or above the store
cues.zh: 商人未必住在店铺楼上，因为他们太有钱了，不会那么做。任何开酒类商店的人都买得起独栋住宅的美国梦。住在店铺附近或楼上的人

cues.en: are the clerks
cues.zh: 是店员

cues.en: and the waiters
cues.zh: 和服务员

cues.en: and the apprentice pharmacists and all sorts of people, in fact, that if they don't live nearby,
cues.zh: 和见习药剂师以及各种各样的人，事实上，如果他们不住在附近，

cues.en: they have to own cars, which they really can't afford to own because they're not getting paid that much. And they also plug up the parking lot by having to commute there. Why not permit them to live above the store, either in this... In the shopping center pattern or even in the, Stop and Shop or whatever your local... I don't know whether it's seven eleven or Circle K. This is a this is a convenience store in the very beautiful and delicate town of Skonset in Nantucket.
cues.zh: 他们就得有车，而他们其实买不起车，因为工资没那么高。而且他们还得通勤到那里，把停车场也塞满了。为什么不让他们住在店铺楼上呢，无论是在这种……购物中心模式里，甚至是在 Stop and Shop 或你们当地的……我不知道是 7-Eleven 还是 Circle K。这是楠塔基特那座非常美丽而精致的城镇 Skonset 里的一家便利店。

cues.en: Then instead of being considered a blight, as a seven eleven would be, it's considered the corner store, perfectly nice place with the people who work there living above.
cues.zh: 于是它不再像 7-Eleven 那样被视为城市败笔，而被看作街角小店，一个相当不错的地方，在那里工作的人就住在楼上。

cues.en: This is Princeton, New Jersey, Palmer Square,
cues.zh: 这里是新泽西州普林斯顿的帕尔默广场，

cues.en: built by a developer as a single shot, administered by a developer as a single shot, extremely
cues.zh: 由同一个开发商一次性建成、由同一个开发商一次性管理，极其

cues.en: profitable retail,
cues.zh: 利润丰厚的零售区，

cues.en: and very, very desirable places to live. In fact, one of the great secrets is how many people love to live above the store.
cues.zh: 而且是非常非常理想的居住地。事实上，最大的秘密之一就是，有多少人喜欢住在店铺楼上。

cues.en: There's a development in Southern New Jersey that had apartments above the store. They sold 90 of them in three days.
cues.zh: 南新泽西有一个开发项目，商铺上方是公寓。他们三天内卖出了90套。

cues.en: In Miami Lakes, in, in Florida, all of the apartments above the stores, which is a new a new development, are rented.
cues.zh: 在佛罗里达的 Miami Lakes，所有商铺上方的公寓——这是一个新开发项目——都已租出去了。

cues.en: In, Hyde Park Village in,
cues.zh: 在，Hyde Park Village，在，

cues.en: in, Tampa, the same thing. The apartments above the store, constantly rented. And the same thing in Reston. The only part of Reston that did well were the apartments above the store in Lake Ann.
cues.zh: 在 Tampa，也一样。商铺上方的公寓一直租得很好。Reston 也一样。Reston 唯一表现好的部分，就是 Lake Ann 商铺上方的公寓。

cues.en: The other way to provide affordable housing, is the the healthiest possible way to do it.
cues.zh: 提供可负担住房的另一种方式，也是最健康的做法。

cues.en: Backyard cottages, or if you prefer to call them granny flats or garage apartments.
cues.zh: 后院小屋，或者你更愿意叫它们祖母房或车库公寓。

cues.en: You see, this little building,
cues.zh: 你看，这栋小建筑，

cues.en: which is which is is
cues.zh: 也就是，也就是，是

cues.en: here in the back of this house.
cues.zh: 就在这栋房子的后面。

cues.en: Now what is a garage apartment or a granny flat? It's a bedroom that has gravitated
cues.zh: 那么车库公寓或祖母房是什么呢？它是一间卧室，已经挪移

cues.en: from inside the house to become independent
cues.zh: 从房子里面出来，变得独立

cues.en: so that it can enter the rental market.
cues.zh: 从而能够进入租赁市场。

cues.en: See, this nation is full of unused bedrooms. There are millions of unused bedrooms all over, which cannot be rented because they would violate the privacy of the family.
cues.zh: 你看，这个国家到处都是空置的卧室。全国有数百万间空置卧室，却没法出租，因为出租会侵犯家庭的隐私。

cues.en: But if that bedroom were permitted to be separate like this and equipped with a small kitchen,
cues.zh: 但如果允许那间卧室像这样独立出来，再配上一个小厨房，

cues.en: not only could you rent
cues.zh: 你不仅可以把房子租

cues.en: to people,
cues.zh: 给别人，

cues.en: at 2 or $300 a month, but that 2 or $300
cues.zh: 每月收个两三百美元，而且这两三百美元

cues.en: would supplement the mortgage of the principal,
cues.zh: 还能补贴主要

cues.en: owner, which would in turn make it more affordable.
cues.zh: 房主的房贷，这反过来又让住房变得更负担得起。

cues.en: And it's the best kind of affordable housing because it is integrated into the middle class.
cues.zh: 而且这是最好的一种可负担住房，因为它融入了中产阶级社区。

cues.en: So the middle class norms of behavior are applied.
cues.zh: 于是，中产阶级的行为规范就被套用上来。

cues.en: It's not up to the police department to make sure that this person, you know, keeps their stereo low or keeps the the car parked in the right place. It's up to the principal landowner to do it. It's a self policing. It's a privately policed system.
cues.zh: 这不该由警察局来确保这个人把音响音量调低，或者把车停在合适的位置。这该由主要土地所有者来做。这是自我监管，是私人化的治安体系。

cues.en: This has been around since the very first settlements of America. Williamsburg is full of outbuildings.
cues.zh: 从美国最早的定居点开始，这种东西就一直存在。威廉斯堡到处都是附属建筑。

cues.en: But now, and all the way till the twenties, the houses all had these.
cues.zh: 但现在，一直到二十年代，这些房子都有这个。

cues.en: And now they're completely illegal. And planning departments zealously check to make sure that you can't slip in a kitchen anywhere, you know, as if it were gonna be the end of the world.
cues.zh: 现在它们完全是非法的。规划部门还特别积极地检查，确保你没法在任何地方偷偷加个厨房，好像这会世界末日似的。

cues.en: What's happening is that people are afraid of lots becoming duplex lots,
cues.zh: 现在的问题是，人们担心地块会变成双户住宅地块，

cues.en: but that can be easily controlled by maintaining the maximum size to 400 square feet.
cues.zh: 但这很容易控制，只要把最大面积维持在400平方英尺就行。

cues.en: Because if it's at 400 square feet, only a single person or a or a couple can live there, and it doesn't get into the children and all that overload that that it implies. Outbuildings should not only be made legal, they should be encouraged.
cues.zh: 因为如果只有400平方英尺，那只能住一个人或一对夫妇，不会涉及孩子以及随之而来的种种超负荷问题。附属建筑不仅应该合法化，还应该受到鼓励。

cues.en: Now two rules
cues.zh: 现在有两条规则

cues.en: about how to provide affordable housing so that it doesn't turn into a slum.
cues.zh: 关于如何提供经济适用房，又不让它变成贫民窟。

cues.en: Rule number one is it's got to look normal.
cues.zh: 第一条规则是，它看起来必须正常。

cues.en: Do not experiment
cues.zh: 不要做实验

cues.en: on the poor.
cues.zh: 拿穷人做实验。

cues.en: Architects love to experiment on the poor because the poor are presumed to be grateful to have a roof and a bathroom.
cues.zh: 建筑师喜欢拿穷人做实验，因为人们想当然地认为，穷人只要有屋顶和卫生间就会心存感激。

cues.en: And, of course, the middle class won't put up with it because they'll just go buy something that looks normal, so they experiment on the poor. But the problem is that the poor are already insecure enough about, you know, their social situation without looking like an architectural experiment.
cues.zh: 当然，中产阶级不会忍受这种事，因为他们大可以去买看起来正常的东西，所以建筑师就拿穷人做实验。但问题是，穷人对自己的社会处境本来就够缺乏安全感了，更别说还得看起来像一场建筑实验。

cues.en: So they tend to trash the places that look funny.
cues.zh: 所以他们往往会把那些看起来怪怪的地方直接毁掉。

cues.en: Why not provide affordable housing the way we used to? This is in Annapolis.
cues.zh: 为什么不按我们过去的方式来建经济适用房呢？这是在安纳波利斯。

cues.en: Here, on this this house is one of the great historic houses of Annapolis,
cues.zh: 这里，这栋房子是安纳波利斯最了不起的历史建筑之一，

cues.en: a large place with a huge garden.
cues.zh: 地方很大，还带一个巨大的花园。

cues.en: This is a more middle class house, and right next to them are two twelve foot townhouses,
cues.zh: 这是一栋更偏中产阶层的房子，紧挨着它的是两栋十二英尺宽的联排住宅，

cues.en: 12 feet. But they look like the rest of the houses. They have decent materials, decent windows, decent door.
cues.zh: 十二英尺。但它们看起来和其他房子没两样。材料不错，窗户不错，门也不错。

cues.en: It's just that they are smaller.
cues.zh: 只是它们更小。

cues.en: Also,
cues.zh: 另外，

cues.en: it is interspersed
cues.zh: 它们穿插分布，

cues.en: with the middle with with the middle class.
cues.zh: 与中产阶层混在一起。

cues.en: And that's the second rule.
cues.zh: 这就是第二条规则。

cues.en: It is not enough to provide housing that looks normal.
cues.zh: 只提供看起来正常的住房还不够。

cues.en: It is important that you provide it in very small increments interspersed
cues.zh: 重要的是，你要以很小的增量提供，并穿插

cues.en: with market rate housing.
cues.zh: 在市场价住房之间。

cues.en: This is in St. Louis.
cues.zh: 这是在圣路易斯。

cues.en: St. Louis has undergone two generations of experiments in affordable housing.
cues.zh: 圣路易斯经历了两代保障性住房实验。

cues.en: The first one was the high rises,
cues.zh: 第一批是高层楼群，

cues.en: which of course were demolished in that very famous
cues.zh: 它们当然在那场非常著名的

cues.en: in in the seventies.
cues.zh: 七十年代事件中被拆除了。

cues.en: That was a failed experiment. So then they said, we've learned the lesson. We won't put people in townhouses.
cues.zh: 那是个失败的实验。后来他们说，我们吸取教训了。我们不会再把人安排到联排别墅里。

cues.en: We're gonna put them in low rise that looks normal, which they did. Here it is. But this also turned into a slump. The problem is that they put 300 of these in one place. And all it takes is a couple of rotten apples, a couple of people selling drugs, a couple of cars that can't be maintained to have the whole thing degenerate.
cues.zh: 我们会把他们安置在看起来正常的低层住宅里，他们确实这么做了。就是这个。但这里也变成了贫民窟。问题在于，他们把300套这样的住宅集中在一个地方。而只要有几个害群之马，几个卖毒品的人，几辆没法维护的车，整个地方就会败坏。

cues.en: You can't put housing in large increments. It has it has to be scattered
cues.zh: 住房不能大规模集中建设。必须分散。

cues.en: even in small increments.
cues.zh: 哪怕是小规模增量。

cues.en: I mean, especially in small increments.
cues.zh: 我是说，尤其是小规模增量。

cues.en: Two affordable housing units like this are not going to destroy the real estate value of 10 or 20 houses around them. That's the only way it will survive. Any housing that you build on this pattern
cues.zh: 像这样的两套可负担住房，不会毁掉周围十到二十栋房子的房产价值。只有这样，它才能存续。任何按这种模式建造的住房

cues.en: is really a wasted investment because it will go under and it will require maintenance and perhaps even demolition.
cues.zh: 都是浪费投资，因为它会垮掉，需要维护，甚至可能被拆除。

cues.en: How do you intersperse this housing? Because developers will tell you, well, we can't mix incomes. That'll never work. You know, people don't like living with people of different incomes and so forth.
cues.zh: 你要怎么穿插布置这些住房？因为开发商会跟你说，我们不能混合收入群体。那根本行不通。你知道，人们不喜欢和不同收入的人住在一起，等等。

cues.en: Well, the reason they say that is that this is the pattern that they're thinking about. This
cues.zh: 他们这么说的原因，是因为他们想到的是这种模式。这个

cues.en: is what we call a train wreck.
cues.zh: 就是我们所说的灾难现场。

cues.en: Now you're welcome... Or planners are welcome to do housing as erratic as this one, site planning as erratic,
cues.zh: 现在，欢迎你们……或者说，规划者尽可以做出像这个一样杂乱的住房、同样杂乱的场地规划，

cues.en: if it weren't for one thing.
cues.zh: 要不是因为有一件事。

cues.en: And that is that these these apartment buildings that are spinning wild wildly
cues.zh: 而那些旋转得很夸张的公寓楼

cues.en: on their site
cues.zh: 在它们的地块上

cues.en: have... Are incapable of having a front and a back, the discipline of front and back. And it is that discipline of front and back that permits housing to be mixed.
cues.zh: 它们……无法拥有正面和背面，无法做到正背面的区分纪律。而正是这种正背面的区分纪律，才让住宅可以混合。

cues.zh: 看这张航拍照片。

cues.zh: 这是我住的地方。这是佛罗里达州的 Coral Gables，

cues.en: which is the development from the nineteen twenties. It has the highest real estate values in South Florida, the second highest in all of Florida after Palm Beach. It's an open grid to the city. K? That has never been a problem, by the way, in expensive neighborhoods. You don't need to gate people off to to have security
cues.zh: 是上世纪二十年代开发的项目。它拥有南佛罗里达最高的房产价值，在整個佛罗里达州仅次于 Palm Beach。它对城市是开放式的路网。对吧？顺便说一句，在昂贵社区里这从来不是问题。你不需要用门禁把人隔开才有安全感

cues.en: because all you need to do is make authentic neighborhoods they take care of themselves.
cues.zh: 因为你只需要打造真实的社区，它们会自己照顾自己。

cues.en: But that's not what I'm talking about here. What I wanna talk about here is that within a very small,
cues.zh: 但这不是我在这里要说的。我在这里想说的是，在一个非常小的、

cues.en: geographical
cues.zh: 地理

cues.en: distance, which is to say,
cues.zh: 距离内，也就是说，

cues.en: not, in fact, smaller than this pod here, Coral Gables manages to have an avenue
cues.zh: 事实上并不比这里这个小组小，Coral Gables 竟然拥有一条大道，

cues.en: that has 16 story office buildings and apartment buildings and hotels on both sides of this street.
cues.zh: 这条大道两侧有 16 层高的办公楼、公寓楼和酒店。

cues.en: The next street over has apartment buildings of two and three stories, which is to say quite affordable housing, and the next street over has expensive single family houses.
cues.zh: 隔壁那条街是两三层高的公寓楼，也就是相当可负担的住房；再隔壁那条街则是昂贵的独栋住宅。

cues.en: How is this achieved?

cues.en: It's achieved because people relate to their front door. It's their address. It's their stoop. It's their street that means something to them. What happens behind them is of very little importance.

cues.zh: 第二个要素，

cues.zh: 自文艺复兴时期起就为人所知，

cues.zh: 就是高宽比。

cues.zh: 好吗？为了营造场所感，

cues.zh: 你不能超过

cues.zh: 高度。围合墙就是高度。建筑之间的宽度

cues.zh: 就是宽度。

cues.zh: 高宽比不能超过一比六。

cues.zh: 在一个，在一个满是游客、叫 Stewart 的佛罗里达小镇。这种建筑并不比那一种更优越。

cues.zh: 它们都是盒子。区别在于，所有信息

cues.en: that this house is giving is about people.
cues.zh: 这栋房子所传递的，都与人有关。

Now what happens is that that humans are a very gregarious species, and they love people and what they do. They watch each other a lot. This house is full of people activity or potential people activity.
cues.zh: 人们开灯关灯。人们站在窗后。人们把报纸放在门前台阶上。接下来是，人类是非常群居的物种，他们喜欢人以及人的行为。他们经常互相观察。这栋房子充满人的活动，或潜在的人的活动。

cues.en: This one is not. So you get pedestrian life here, and you don't get pedestrian life here. In fact, I happen to know, this is a place called Wellington
cues.zh: 这个不是。所以这里能过步行生活，而这里不能。事实上，我碰巧知道，这地方叫惠灵顿

cues.en: in Florida, where we're now doing the 1,600 acre extension.
cues.zh: 在佛罗里达州，我们现在正在做1600英亩的扩建。

cues.en: The people in Wellington
cues.zh: 惠灵顿的人

cues.en: take drive
cues.zh: 开车

cues.en: to the exercise
cues.zh: 去健身

cues.en: club where they do... Where they use the walking machines. That's actually what they do.
cues.zh: 俱乐部，他们在那里……在那里用走步机。他们实际上就是这么做的。

cues.en: Now, how is that to be achieved? How can you overcome the problem of the garage
cues.zh: 那么，这要怎么实现？你怎么解决车库的问题

cues.en: when you have a small lot? I mean, after all, if you have a 50 foot lot and you have two parked cars, that's taking up 50% of your frontage. No architect can overcome that.
cues.zh: 当你只有一小块地时？我是说，毕竟，如果你有50英尺宽的地块，还停着两辆车，那就占了50%的临街面。没有建筑师能解决这个问题。

cues.en: It will eat up the frontage. What you need are alleys or lanes like this.
cues.zh: 这会占掉临街面。你需要的是像这样的巷道或小路。

cues.en: The old system of alleys and lanes permits people to park from the rear. That's why the old neighborhoods here in San Antonio feel so much... Look so much better. It's not that the housing is necessarily superior because it's actually not that different. Some of the new housing looks pretty good. It's just that the old housing is not showing a high percentage of garage doors. So they're they're automatically,
cues.zh: 旧式的巷道和小路系统让人们可以从后面停车。这就是为什么圣安东尼奥这里的老街区感觉……看起来好得多。并不是说老房子一定更好，因为其实差别没那么大。有些新住宅看起来相当不错。只是老住宅的车库门比例没那么高。所以它们会自动——

cues.en: they subconsciously
cues.zh: 会下意识地

cues.en: would consider them friendlier.
cues.zh: 觉得它们更友好。

cues.en: This, not only the cars in the back, but the trash cans in the back are a great asset, and the infrastructure,
cues.zh: 这——不只是后面的汽车，还有后面的垃圾桶——都是很大的资产，还有基础设施，

cues.en: especially the cables and the pipes.
cues.zh: 尤其是线缆和管道。

cues.en: When they're to the rear, you don't have to mangle the trees in front. The... You know, with the... And even when they're buried, even when the cables are buried,
cues.zh: 当它们位于后面时，你就不必糟蹋前面的树木。这个……你知道，有了……而且即使它们被埋在地下，即使线缆被埋在地下，

cues.en: as they often are these days, if they're in the front, they're preventing the planting for... Of trees to occur there, which immediately widens the street. And as you know, or as I said earlier, the narrower the street, the more popular it is. In fact, I have an entire series of slides
cues.zh: 就像如今经常这样，如果它们在前面，就会妨碍在那里种……种树，这会立刻让街道变宽。而且如你所知，或者像我之前说的，街道越窄，越受欢迎。事实上，我有一整套幻灯片

cues.en: that show how in every city,
cues.zh: 展示了在每个城市，

cues.en: the highest real estate value coincides with the narrowest street. It's exactly the opposite of what developers think. It's a remarkable situation.
cues.zh: 最高的房地产价值恰好与最窄的街道重合。这跟开发商的看法完全相反。这是个很值得注意的情况。

cues.en: The most elegant shopping street, the most elegant living street in Boston, in San Francisco, in Miami,
cues.zh: 波士顿、旧金山、迈阿密最优雅的购物街、最优雅的居住街道，

cues.en: the narrowest is the one with the highest real estate value. People love space, love tight spaces.
cues.zh: 最窄的反而地产价值最高。人们喜欢空间，也喜欢紧凑空间。

cues.en: Where is the money for lanes or alleys to come from?
cues.zh: 修车道或小巷的钱从哪儿来？

cues.en: Well, the suburbs are full
cues.zh: 嗯，郊区满是

cues.en: of wasted money.
cues.zh: 浪费掉的钱。

cues.en: Why in the world was this developer,
cues.zh: 这位开发商到底为什么

cues.en: forced to build a collector street?
cues.zh: 被迫修建一条集散街道？

cues.en: Whatever happened to the old system of having a street that had cars and houses on it? Why must this street be built and then this additional street be built also? This is a complete waste of money,
cues.zh: 过去那种街上既有汽车又有房子的老办法哪去了？为什么非得建了这条街，还要再建那条额外的街？这完全是浪费钱，

cues.en: which can be used in other ways. Besides,
cues.zh: 这些钱本可以用在别处。再说，

cues.en: this, by being,
cues.zh: 这种街道，因为

cues.en: detailed,
cues.zh: 细节精致，

cues.en: having the geometries
cues.zh: 又具有

cues.en: of a
cues.zh: 一条

cues.en: highway, means that people speed.
cues.zh: 高速公路的几何形态，就意味着人们会超速。

cues.en: So first they build these high speed streets, then they put speed bumps to hobble them. You know? Why not use the natural system in which the natural width, narrowness of the street, and the parked cars
cues.zh: 所以他们先建了这些高速街道，然后又放减速带把它们废掉。你懂吧？为什么不利用自然系统——街道天然的宽度、狭窄程度，还有停着的车

cues.en: automatically make people go slowly? That's the old economical system.
cues.zh: 会自动让人慢下来？这才是古老又经济的方式。

cues.en: One other detail about this.
cues.zh: 关于这一点，还有一个细节。

cues.en: It is not enough to just require open space, like many codes have 30 open space. If all you ask is open space, the developers will give you this drivel on the edges, which they don't want anyway,
cues.zh: 光要求开放空间是不够的，比如很多规范都要求30%的开放空间。如果你只要求开放空间，开发商就会在边缘塞给你这种垃圾，反正他们自己也不想要，

cues.en: which is perfectly useless.
cues.zh: 那完全没用。

cues.en: You should define your open space as accurately as you define your parking lots. Open spaces have three different... Or actually four different categories.
cues.zh: 你应该像定义停车场那样，准确地定义你的开放空间。开放空间有三类……其实应该说是四类。

cues.en: Squares,
cues.zh: 广场，

cues.en: greens,
cues.zh: 绿地，

cues.en: parks, and green belts. And each of them has a very precise definition.
cues.zh: 公园和绿化带。每一类都有非常精确的定义。

cues.en: And they should be as closely coded as parking lots are coded. A square is a very specific animal, which if it is gonna be used, it needs to be precisely designed, including it should not have an excessive size. The squares that work best are smaller squares.
cues.zh: 它们也应该像停车场那样被严格编码规范。广场是一种很特殊的东西；如果要使用它，就必须精确设计，包括不能做得过大。效果最好的广场，是较小的广场。

cues.en: Plant... They're... They have parking and paving requirements,
cues.zh: 工厂……它们……它们有停车和铺装要求，

cues.en: which should be very, very precisely enunciated
cues.zh: 这些要求应该被非常、非常精确地阐明

cues.en: in a traditional code. Open space, this
cues.zh: 在传统规范中。开放空间，这

cues.en: is really... It's it's just a maintenance problem, and it it it really does not form a focus of society.
cues.zh: 其实……它它只是个维护问题，而且它它它真的不构成社会的关注焦点。

cues.en: Another aspect which seems to be inoffensive,
cues.zh: 另一个看似无害的方面，

cues.en: but it turns out to be of crucial importance,
cues.zh: 结果却至关重要，

cues.en: is this mania
cues.zh: 就是这种狂热，

cues.en: that that planners have now developed for the dead worm street system.
cues.zh: 规划师们如今对死胡同式街道系统发展出的那种狂热。

cues.en: Like this. Why is it that this is so important
cues.zh: 就像这样。为什么这一点如此重要

cues.en: to planners and developers
cues.zh: 对规划师和开发商来说

cues.en: to the extent that, for example, twice we have been summarily fired
cues.zh: 以至于，比如，我们有两次被立即解雇

cues.en: by developers for doing straight line
cues.zh: 被开发商，因为采用直线

cues.en: layouts.
cues.zh: 布局。

cues.en: Even though every
cues.zh: 尽管每一个

cues.en: single wonderful city and village in the world has straight streets.
cues.zh: 世上美妙的城市和村庄都有笔直的街道。

cues.en: And all the boring suburbs in the world have curvilinear ones.
cues.zh: 而世上所有无聊的郊区却都是曲线街道。

cues.en: All the places we love to visit have straight streets. And yet, it is anathema to do it.
cues.zh: 我们爱去的地方都有笔直的街道。可这么做却成了禁忌。

cues.en: If you want to waste a lot of money doing these hyper expensive curvy streets, which in addition to that are completely confusing,
cues.zh: 如果你想浪费一大笔钱，去修这些超级昂贵、弯弯曲曲的街道，而且它们还让人完全摸不着头脑，

cues.en: the primary the primary experience of being in the suburb in a layout like this is the stress of being lost.
cues.zh: 身处这种布局的郊区，最主要的体验就是迷路带来的焦虑。

cues.en: There's no way around it. That's what it feels like. You need specific instructions.
cues.zh: 这没法回避。感觉就是这样。你需要具体的指引。

cues.en: First left, second right. And if you make the mistake or it's night, you're really in terrible shape.
cues.zh: 第一个路口左转，第二个路口右转。要是你走错了，或者赶上晚上，那你就真的惨了。

cues.en: Why is this so important? Well, it's important
cues.zh: 这为什么这么重要？嗯，它很重要

cues.en: because it terminates vistas.
cues.zh: 因为它终结了远景。

cues.en: Apparently or correctly,
cues.zh: 显然，或者更准确地说，

cues.en: people do not like to look down the street and have the vista terminate somewhere in the haze in the prairie. That is not a satisfactory feeling.
cues.zh: 人们不喜欢沿街望去，视线却在草原的薄雾中消失。那种感觉并不令人满意。

cues.en: And when you when you curve the street, it actually closes the vista in a systematic manner. In an unthinking manner, it is vaguely pleasant.
cues.zh: 而当你——当你把街道弯曲时，它其实会有系统地收束远景。这种不假思索的做法，隐约令人愉悦。

cues.en: But it's pleasant in the way that elevator music is pleasant.
cues.zh: 但这种愉悦，就像电梯音乐带来的愉悦一样。

cues.en: You can't remember what it does, and that's the problem. There's no system of orientations.
cues.zh: 你记不住它是干什么的，问题就在这儿。这里没有一套方向参照系统。

cues.en: Those of you who are planners have read Kevin Lynch's
cues.zh: 你们当中做规划的人读过 Kevin Lynch 的

cues.en: image of the city, and it talks about how important it is for people to orient themselves to know where they are by using landmarks.
cues.zh: 《城市意象》，书里讲到，人们通过地标来辨明自己身在何处、建立方向感，这有多重要。

cues.en: In a layout like this, it is completely impossible to achieve landmarks because the eye never rests on anything. Before the architect can respond,
cues.zh: 像这样的布局，根本不可能形成地标，因为视线从不在任何东西上停留。还没等建筑师作出回应，

cues.en: you've been taken away and taken away and nothing. You cannot focus on anything.
cues.zh: 你就被带走了，又被带走了，结果什么都没有。你根本无法聚焦在任何东西上。

cues.en: It is not natural,
cues.zh: 这不自然，

cues.en: as you can see.
cues.zh: 如你所见。

cues.en: In fact, if you wanna see how to use the land intelligently and in an ecologically sound
cues.zh: 事实上，如果你想看看如何明智且生态友好地利用土地

cues.en: manner that that is very, accurate about where the wetlands are and the subtleties, see what the farmers do.
cues.zh: 并且非常准确地把握湿地的位置和细微之处，那就看看农民是怎么做的。

cues.en: Whenever we have studied the layout of farmers, the small deflections and so forth that occur,
cues.zh: 每当我们研究农民的布局，以及其中出现的细微偏转等等，

cues.en: they... This is really what the land requires,
cues.zh: 它们……这才是土地真正需要的，

cues.en: not this artificial
cues.zh: 而不是这种人为的

cues.en: curving.
cues.zh: 弯曲。

cues.en: The way landmarks are to be used is not by making curvilinear streets,
cues.zh: 地标的使用方式并不是铺设曲线街道，

cues.en: but by terminating vistas with memorable buildings.
cues.zh: 而是用令人难忘的建筑来作为景观视线的终点。

cues.en: Those cities that we remember to be wonderful cities
cues.zh: 那些我们记忆中很棒的城市

cues.en: often have their important buildings in important locations.
cues.zh: 往往把重要建筑放在重要位置。

cues.en: This is Charleston, South Carolina,
cues.zh: 这是南卡罗来纳州的查尔斯顿，

cues.en: where this important street ends there. Washington DC
cues.zh: 这条重要街道在那里到头。华盛顿特区

cues.en: is the primary city in The United States in which the vistas are terminated by important buildings. But Annapolis and and,
cues.zh: 是美国最主要的一座城市，那里的景观视野都由重要建筑收束。但安纳波利斯，以及，以及，

cues.en: and Williamsburg
cues.zh: 以及威廉斯堡

cues.en: and many of the Texan and Florida courthouse towns have terminated vistas like... You have quite a few here in San Antonio when streets deflect.
cues.zh: 以及得克萨斯和佛罗里达的许多法院城镇，都有这种以重要建筑收束视野的布局……在圣安东尼奥，街道转折时你也能看到不少。

cues.en: In fact, when you look at an old planning book for up to 1930,
cues.zh: 事实上，翻开一本1930年以前的旧规划书，

cues.en: there's page after page of intersections that look like this,
cues.zh: 里面有一页又一页像这样的交叉路口，

cues.en: in which what the plan... What the book is is proposing is all sorts of different ways by which the vista
cues.zh: 书里提出的方案……这本书提出的是各种不同的方式，让景观

cues.en: gives a special location so that architects can respond in a memorable way
cues.zh: 获得一个特殊的位置，好让建筑师能以令人难忘的方式

cues.en: to the vista. Now, we have given... This particular book had over 20 of these. We gave it to our traffic engineer, and the traffic engineer determined that every single one was illegal. We
cues.zh: 回应这处景观。我们给了……这本特别的书里有20多个这样的例子。我们把它交给交通工程师，交通工程师判定每一个都不合法。我们

cues.en: also traveled with our traffic engineer,
cues.zh: 也和我们的交通工程师一起出行过，

cues.en: and he always finds that all of these are illegal.
cues.zh: 而他总是发现所有这些都不合法。

cues.en: Now, we point out and say, but my dear sir, no one has crashed into this in a hundred and fifty years. You see? That doesn't matter. It's not in the books.
cues.zh: 现在我们指出并说：可是先生，一百五十年了都没人撞上过它。你明白吗？那不重要。规范里没写。

cues.en: The assumption that is being made
cues.zh: 这里所做的假设是

cues.en: is that this, instead of being a narrow street in which cars go slowly by virtue of the parked cars and the smaller dimension,
cues.zh: 这里不是一条窄街——因为停着车、尺度又小，汽车本来会慢慢通过，

cues.en: what the engineers assume is that this is a micro highway.
cues.zh: 而工程师们假设，这是一条微型高速公路。

cues.en: And, of course, in a standard Department of Transportation section, people will speed and they will hit that church.
cues.zh: 当然，在交通部的标准路段设计中，人们会超速，然后撞上那座教堂。

cues.en: The drunk at midnight will actually hit that church sooner or later. See, this is not... You can't just do parts of it. You can't have intersections like these unless you, at the same time, reduce
cues.zh: 半夜的醉汉迟早会撞上那座教堂。你看，这不是……你不能只做其中一部分。你不能有这样的路口，除非同时缩减

cues.en: the street section so that people slow up. It's very dangerous to do traditional urbanism on a partial basis because it tends to explode.
cues.zh: 街道断面，让人们慢下来。零散地做传统城市主义非常危险，因为很容易出大乱子。

cues.en: You need to have the entire kit of parts. The entire kit of parts works beautifully.
cues.zh: 你需要有完整的一套构件。整套构件组合起来效果非常好。

cues.en: Now this is a very important tool, determination of vistas,
cues.zh: 这是个非常重要的工具——确定景观视廊，

cues.en: because it means that our civic buildings, which are no longer,
cues.zh: 因为它意味着我们的市政建筑，它们已不再——

cues.en: we no longer have the model, We no longer have the money to build beautiful civic buildings. You know, we're we're no longer a rich country.
cues.zh: 我们不再有那种范本，也不再有钱去建漂亮的市政建筑。你知道，我们不再是个富裕国家了。

cues.en: So we build we build normal dignified civic buildings, but they can be enormously enhanced by giving them honorable locations at the end of vistas.
cues.zh: 所以我们建普通但庄重的市政建筑，但只要把它们放在景观视廊尽头的重要位置，就能大大提升它们。

cues.en: We just can't operate as planners
cues.zh: 我们作为规划师根本无法运作

cues.en: unless we're permitted to terminate vistas with buildings. What happens is that the art of urban planning is removed from us. We can't act. We can no longer make beautiful cities unless intersections like these are recovered. It's of crucial importance.
cues.zh: 除非允许我们用建筑收束远景。结果就是，城市规划的艺术被从我们手中夺走。我们无法行动。除非恢复这样的路口，否则我们再也造不出美丽的城市。这至关重要。

cues.en: Another aspect of pedestrian life is only a detail,
cues.zh: 步行生活的另一个方面只是一个细节，

cues.en: but it is as important as any other element.
cues.zh: 但它和其他任何元素一样重要。

cues.en: Notice
cues.zh: 注意

cues.en: that in cities where there's a pedestrian life, the curb radius is relatively small.
cues.zh: 在有步行生活的城市里，路缘半径相对较小。

cues.en: In this case, in Boston, it's an eight foot radius.
cues.zh: 在这个案例中，波士顿这里是8英尺半径。

cues.en: It means that the pedestrian moving down the sidewalk,
cues.zh: 也就是说，沿人行道行走的行人，

cues.en: when that pedestrian arrives at a 24 foot paving,
cues.zh: 当这个行人到达24英尺宽的铺装路面时，

cues.en: that crossing distance is only 24 feet,
cues.zh: 过街距离只有24英尺，

cues.en: which is a doable distance.
cues.zh: 这是可以走过去的距离。

cues.en: In the current mode of increasing curb radii, in this case, it's a Miami residential neighborhood with 25,
cues.zh: 在当前增大路缘半径的做法下，这个案例是迈阿密的一个住宅区，路缘半径是25英尺，

cues.en: what happens is that the pedestrian moving down the sidewalk,
cues.zh: 结果就是，沿人行道行走的行人，

cues.en: instead of just crossing the 24 feet of paving, has to cross 48 feet of paving,
cues.zh: 不再只需穿过24英尺的铺装路面，而必须穿过48英尺的铺装路面，

cues.en: which means that the window of opportunity for crossing... If this one can be crossed, for example, in seven seconds,
cues.zh: 这意味着过街的时间窗口……如果这一处能在比如7秒内穿过，

cues.en: this one needs to be crossed in fourteen seconds. It needs fourteen seconds to cross it. And, of course, that instance of the fourteen second gap occurs much more seldom than the seven second gap.
cues.zh: 这一处则需要14秒才能穿过。它需要14秒才能通过。而且当然，14秒间隙出现的频率远低于7秒间隙。

cues.en: And so you tend to have pedestrian life die when this happens when this happens.
cues.zh: 于是，当这种情况发生、这种情况发生时，步行生活往往就消亡了。

cues.en: The other thing that happens is that the cars don't have to slow up. This guy is tilting his car making that turn. He's not even touching the brake.
cues.zh: 另一件事是，汽车不必减速。这家伙转弯时把车身倾斜。他甚至连刹车都没碰。

cues.en: What has happened in The United States is that traffic engineering standards,
cues.zh: 在美国发生的情况是，交通工程标准，

cues.en: which used to have a full range from 15 miles an hour to 85 or, god knows, a 100 miles an hour, each track... Each speed having a whole series of geometrical requirements, centerline radii, curb radii, and so forth. Back in the nineteen fifties or sixties, the whole bottom end
cues.zh: 这些标准过去覆盖从每小时15英里到85英里，或者天晓得，每小时100英里的完整范围，每一档……每种速度都有一整套几何要求，中心线半径、路缘半径等等。早在二十世纪五六十年代，整个底端

cues.en: of the manual was removed,
cues.zh: 手册的这一部分被删掉了，

cues.en: and we no longer can design streets that are less than 35 miles an hour.
cues.zh: 于是我们再也无法设计时速低于每小时35英里的街道了。

cues.en: That is the fundamental problem that is happening here. And in fact, the push is now still in the other direction. In Miami now, the Public Works Department is proposing 40 foot right of ways,
cues.zh: 这就是这里正在发生的根本问题。而事实上，现在的推动方向仍然相反。在迈阿密，公共工程部正提议40英尺的路权，

cues.en: which means you can do that easily at 40 miles an hour, perhaps even at 50 for a decent driver. What does 50 mile an hour turns have to do with a residential neighborhood?
cues.zh: 这意味着以40英里的时速可以轻松做到，对技术不错的司机甚至50英里也行。50英里时速的转弯和住宅区有什么关系？

cues.en: What's happening is that the traffic engineers are considered the solution to our traffic problems, the only solution to our traffic problems, and they're being given an absolutely free hand to make the traffic flow as quickly as possible and as efficiently as possible at the expense of other issues such as public life.
cues.zh: 现在的情况是，交通工程师被视为我们交通问题的解决方案，而且是唯一方案，他们被完全放手让交通尽可能快速、高效地流动，牺牲了公共生活等其他问题。

cues.en: They have, at this moment, no natural enemies.
cues.zh: 目前，它们没有天敌。

cues.en: So like any any predator,
cues.zh: 所以，就像任何捕食者一样，

cues.en: in that condition,
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，

cues.en: there is nothing to stop them from, in fact, doing more and more of this. Fortunately, I had been asked to lecture tomorrow at the National Convention of the Institute of Traffic Engineers for three hours. So
cues.zh: 实际上，没有什么能阻止它们越来越多地这么做。幸运的是，我被邀请明天在交通工程师协会全国大会上讲三个小时。所以

cues.en: it is... But it's... I assure you, it is about the first opposition they will have met in years.
cues.zh: 这是……但这是……我向你保证，这差不多是它们多年来第一次遇到反对。

cues.en: They are like gods
cues.zh: 它们就像神一样

cues.en: because, you know, they are considered the solution and the only solution to the problem. What is it like? What are the what are the economic implications
cues.zh: 因为，你知道，它们被视为解决方案，而且是这个问题的唯一解决方案。那是什么样子？都有哪些……都有哪些经济影响

cues.en: of this kind of investment in highways?
cues.zh: 对高速公路的这种投资来说？

cues.en: Here on the left is the illustration on the cover
cues.zh: 左边是封面上的插图

cues.en: of the Florida...
cues.zh: 佛罗里达……

cues.en: Of the of the annual report of the Florida Department of Transportation.
cues.zh: 佛罗里达交通部年度报告的。

cues.en: This is obviously what they have in mind for us in Florida.
cues.zh: 这显然就是佛罗里达方面为我们设想的方案。

cues.en: Now, what has been achieved here is something which is extraordinary. They have turned a little old urban four laner, just a four lane street going through going through an urbanized area, into a highway,
cues.zh: 现在，这里所实现的东西非同寻常。他们把一条老旧的城区四车道——一条穿过城市化地区的四车道街道——变成了一条公路，

cues.en: you know, by these enormous
cues.zh: 你懂的，靠这些巨大的

cues.en: high speed
cues.zh: 高速

cues.en: geometries that have been applied.
cues.zh: 几何线形。

cues.en: As a result of this, not only has a lot of land been consumed and a lot of money been consumed, but the real estate value on either side has been has been actually devastated
cues.zh: 结果，不仅消耗了大量土地和资金，两侧的房地产价值实际上也遭到了严重破坏

cues.en: by the perceived... Actually, the reality of high speed traffic. All of these things along the edge, in fact, have lower real estate value.
cues.zh: 因为人们感知到的……其实是高速交通的现实。事实上，边缘沿线的所有这些，房地产价值都更低。

cues.en: Take an alternate model. This is Paris.
cues.zh: 换个模式。这是巴黎。

cues.en: And I could show you slides of San Francisco or slides of Washington.
cues.zh: 我还可以给你们看旧金山或华盛顿的幻灯片。

cues.en: This is a... This is a... This is... The difference is, I should go back to this, is that this is a highway,
cues.zh: 这是……这是……这是……区别在于，我得回到这一点，这是一条公路，

cues.en: and this is an avenue.
cues.zh: 而这是一条大道。

cues.zh: 公路在乡村自有其位置。

cues.en: But whenever
cues.zh: 但每当

cues.en: a highway enters a city, it should lose its high speed geometries and become an avenue. An avenue has entirely different requirements.
cues.zh: 公路一进入城市，就应该丢掉高速几何特征，变成一条大道。大道有完全不同的要求。

cues.zh: 注意，这里有四条高速车道，

cues.en: two
cues.zh: 两条
