cues.zh: 低速车道，

cues.en: and six lines of parking,
cues.zh: 还有六排停车位，

cues.en: plus trees,
cues.zh: 再加上树木，

cues.en: sidewalks,
cues.zh: 人行道，

cues.en: and buildings,
cues.zh: 以及建筑，

cues.en: and people who consider it perfectly fine to cross and perfectly fine to sit in a cafe and have a nice cup of coffee. This is not a person that considers himself unfortunate to be there. On the contrary, very fortunate to be there.
cues.zh: 还有那些人：他们觉得横穿完全没问题，坐在咖啡馆里喝杯好咖啡也完全没问题。这不是一个觉得自己不幸身在那里的人。恰恰相反，他非常幸运能在那里。

cues.en: How did Paris pay for its infrastructure? Because Paris was entirely reconstructed in the nineteenth century without any tax dollars or tax francs or whatever it was they had at the time. The way they did it is by building avenues like these, which were so elegant and so desirable that they increased real estate value on the side. First, they condemned land, then they built the avenue, then they sold it to developers, and with the value added, they paid for the infrastructure. Not only the streets, but the sewers and the schools. All of that, and the new water system was paid for by this system. So instead of destroying real estate value, they enhance real estate value. Everything
cues.zh: 巴黎是怎么为基础设施买单的？因为巴黎在19世纪被彻底重建，却没有花任何税款——不管是美元还是法郎，或者当时他们用的什么货币。他们的办法是修建像这样的林荫大道，它们优雅又令人向往，顺带抬高了周边的房地产价值。他们先征收土地，再修建大道，然后卖给开发商，凭借增值收益支付了基础设施的费用。不只是道路，还有下水道和学校。所有这些，以及新的供水系统，都是靠这套机制买单的。所以他们不是摧毁房地产价值，而是提升房地产价值。你在这里看到的

cues.en: that you see here
cues.zh: 一切细节

cues.en: in detail is illegal now.
cues.zh: 如今都是违法的。

cues.en: The distance to the tree, the cars parked,
cues.zh: 到树的距离、停放的汽车，

cues.en: this this system of the
cues.zh: 这个，这个系统

cues.en: of the service way with only this much, distance between the two, everything here is illegal. You can't do it. Despite the evidence that a city of 11,000,000
cues.zh: 服务通道的，两者之间只有这么点距离，这里的一切都是违法的。你不能这么做。尽管有证据表明，一座有 1100 万

cues.en: people,
cues.zh: 人口的城市，

cues.en: it works perfectly for them. And these are not some weird Europeans. You know? These perfectly modern people that know exactly what they're doing. But we're not permitted to do this any longer.
cues.zh: 这套做法对他们完全行得通。而且这些人不是什么古怪的欧洲人。你知道吗？这些是完完全全的现代人，很清楚自己在做什么。但我们不再被允许这样做了。

cues.en: We can only do that.
cues.zh: 我们只能这么做。

cues.en: What does it do to... And how are intersections
cues.zh: 它会对……产生什么影响？还有，交叉口是

cues.en: handled? Well,
cues.zh: 怎么处理的？嗯，

cues.en: this is the old system. This is Washington DC.
cues.zh: 这是旧系统。这里是华盛顿特区。

cues.en: This intersection here has tremendous capacity to distribute traffic.
cues.zh: 这里的这个交叉口有极强的交通分流能力。

cues.en: It also has the capacity to make a wonderful
cues.zh: 它还能打造一个美妙的

cues.en: park in the center and to make fantastic elegant building sites that can be sold for a high real estate return.
cues.zh: 中央公园，并打造绝佳而优雅的建筑地块，这些地块能以高额房地产回报出售。

cues.en: All of this in an area about the same size as this... As one quarter of a cloverleaf.
cues.zh: 而这一切都位于一片大约和这个……和一座苜蓿叶式立交的四分之一差不多大的区域里。

cues.en: This area that modern traffic engineering requires is a 120
cues.zh: 现代交通工程所需的这片区域有 120

cues.en: acres.
cues.zh: 英亩。

cues.en: That's the size of Renaissance Florence.
cues.zh: 这相当于文艺复兴时期佛罗伦萨的大小。

cues.en: Every time you see one of these, you know, that's what is being taken out of commission.
cues.zh: 每当你看到其中一处，你知道，这就是被停用的东西。

cues.en: The amount of wastage that is that is implied by this is not only the $7,000,000
cues.zh: 这背后隐含的浪费，不仅是那 700 万美元

cues.en: it cost to build one of these, excluding land acquisition cost. It is not only... It is the taking out of the land and the reduction of real estate value that occurs all along its edges. All of these units rent for less, and mostly, you wanna have parking lots on them.
cues.zh: 建一个这样的设施要花这些钱，还不包括征地成本。这不仅是……它还占用了土地，并导致其边缘沿线房地产贬值。所有这些单元的租金都更低，而且大多数情况下，你会想在上面建停车场。

cues.en: It's a fantastically stupid way to do things. You know what you gain? Ten seconds on the way home
cues.zh: 这做事方式蠢得离谱。你知道能换来什么吗？回家路上省十秒。

cues.en: in your commute home as if that mattered when you were commuting an hour and a half anyway.
cues.zh: 就在你通勤回家的路上，说得好像这很重要似的，反正你本来就要通勤一个半小时。

cues.en: But that's what you gain. You have the pleasure of not even touching your brake as you make that curve.
cues.zh: 但这就是你得到的。过那个弯时，你甚至不用碰刹车，还能享受这种快感。

cues.en: This comes from a period in America when we were so wealthy that we were permitted to be dumb. For forty years, we have done planning,
cues.zh: 这源于美国的一个时期，那时我们富得可以允许自己犯傻。四十年来，我们一直在做规划，

cues.en: the planning of the rich and the stupid.
cues.zh: 富人和蠢人的规划。

cues.en: Now, fortunately,
cues.zh: 现在，幸运的是，

cues.en: we no longer have the money. This is no longer a rich country. You might have noticed that.
cues.zh: 我们不再有钱了。这不再是一个富裕国家。你可能已经注意到了。

cues.en: It happens. There are headlines in the newspaper every day. There's no money for anything. We have now gone back to be a poor country,
cues.zh: 这种事会发生。报纸上每天都有头条。什么事都没钱。我们现在又回到了穷国，

cues.en: which is fine because we were a poor country for the first hundred and fifty years of our existence. And in those years, when we were a poor country, we were smart. This was a this was a poor, smart country, and we used to do things like this. And we... All we have to do, not feel sorry for ourselves that we're now poor, but simply get smart again. This, in many ways, was a better world than this one.
cues.zh: 这没关系，因为我们存在的前一百五十年一直都是穷国。而在那些年，当我们还是穷国时，我们很聪明。这是一个贫穷但聪明的国家，我们过去会做这样的事。而我们……我们要做的，不是因为现在穷了就自怨自艾，而是重新变聪明。从很多方面说，那是一个比现在更好的世界。

cues.en: Some people that suffer,
cues.zh: 有些人会受苦，

cues.en: specific people that suffer or benefit from traditional urbanism,
cues.zh: 具体来说，有些人会因传统城市主义而受苦或受益，

cues.en: police departments benefit.
cues.zh: 警察部门就是受益者。

cues.en: This is one of the great hopeful signs or hopeful interventions
cues.zh: 这是最令人充满希望的迹象或干预措施之一，

cues.en: in police practice, which is the patrolman on the beat. Washington and New York have instituted this.
cues.zh: 在警察实务领域，也就是巡警在辖区内步行巡逻。华盛顿和纽约已经推行了这种做法。

cues.en: Instead of responding to crime in patrol cars, policemen are assigned several city blocks, and they walk it. And they get to know the people, and they can tell that they they... They're able to identify crime before it happens. New York City reported,
cues.zh: 警察不再开着巡逻车应对犯罪，而是被分配到几个城市街区，步行巡逻。他们能认识当地居民，也能看出……他们能在犯罪发生前就识别出来。纽约市报告称，

cues.en: last last week in the New York Times that crime had had dropped 10% in New York, which is remarkable,
cues.zh: 上周《纽约时报》报道，纽约的犯罪率下降了10%，这很了不起，

cues.en: and it might have something to do with these people. By the way, the cops like it. They like to do this. This can't be done in cul de sacs. It's actually technically impossible to do this.
cues.zh: 这可能和这些人有关。顺便说一句，警察喜欢这样，他们乐意这么做。这种事在死胡同式街区里做不到，技术上根本不可能。

cues.en: Developers.
cues.zh: 开发者们。

cues.en: The most sophisticated developers of Florida are Vida.
cues.zh: 佛罗里达最老练的开发商是 Vida。

cues.en: One that get the very best marketing advice, the most expensive, the best, the most thorough marketing advice. What they'd find time after time after time is that the hometown is what sells real estate. Villages, towns, town centers, neighborhoods, it is these words. If developers deliver this, they have absolutely no problem selling.
cues.zh: 就算拿到最好的营销建议——最贵的、最好的、最周全的营销建议，他们一次又一次会发现：真正能卖房地产的是家乡。村庄、城镇、城镇中心、社区，就是这些词。如果开发商能做到这一点，卖房绝对没问题。

cues.en: Other people who suffer,
cues.zh: 其他受苦的人，

cues.en: senior citizens.
cues.zh: 老年人。

cues.en: Florida is full of people who have gone to retire in Florida, in suburban
cues.zh: 佛罗里达到处都是已经去佛罗里达退休的人，住在郊区

cues.en: neighborhoods
cues.zh: 社区

cues.en: or in golf course communities. What they don't realize
cues.zh: 或者住在高尔夫球场社区。他们没有意识到

cues.en: is that is that they need to re retire.
cues.zh: 就是他们需要再次退休。

cues.en: Because what happens is that as soon as they lose their driver's license, which happens when their eyes go bad, not when their minds go bad or when they get physically in bad shape, but when their eyes go bad, they can no longer lead an independent existence.
cues.zh: 因为一旦他们失去驾照——这发生在眼睛不行的时候，而不是头脑不行或身体变差的时候，而是眼睛不行的时候——他们就再也不能独立生活了。

cues.en: And they do two things. They either go back to New Jersey. There's a fantastic out migration from Florida where they go back to where they started, or they go into specialized retirement communities, which are dreadful places usually, where everything is taken care of. Wherever traditional neighborhoods exist,
cues.zh: 他们要么做两件事：要么搬回新泽西——佛罗里达有一波惊人的反向迁出潮，人们回到最初来的地方；要么住进专门的退休社区，那些地方通常很糟糕，一切都被安排妥当。而在传统街区仍然存在的地方，

cues.en: gentlemen like this one can get to be very, very old and still live independently because they can get to their daily needs by walking. This is in in, this is in, Country Club Plaza in Kansas City, which is a development which is done like a traditional neighborhood. Wonderfully successful place.
cues.zh: 像这位先生一样的年长男性可以活到很大年纪，依然独立生活，因为步行就能满足日常所需。这是堪萨斯城的乡村俱乐部广场，一个按传统街区方式开发的社区。非常成功的地方。

cues.en: The seniors suffer and they really... They don't properly identify it. By the way, seniors,
cues.zh: 老年人很受罪，而且他们真的……他们并没有正确意识到这一点。顺便说一句，老年人，

cues.en: North Carolina did a... South Carolina did a study recently, must have been this year, about where where people would prefer to retire. 65%
cues.zh: 北卡罗来纳做了个……南卡罗来纳最近做了一项研究，肯定是今年做的，关于人们更愿意去哪里退休。65%

cues.en: wanted to retire to small towns.
cues.zh: 想退休后搬到小城镇。

cues.en: I don't know how many wanted to retire to golf course communities, but all I can tell you is that of the people who retire in golf course communities, only 27% play golf.
cues.zh: 我不知道有多少人想退休后住到高尔夫球场社区，但我能告诉你的是，在退休后住进高尔夫球场社区的人里，只有27%打高尔夫。

cues.en: And those are the ones within golf course communities. What people really want are towns. They're just not being provided yet by developers.
cues.zh: 这些还都只是高尔夫球场社区里的。人们真正想要的是城镇，只是开发商还没提供出来。

cues.en: Other people who suffer, and these might be the greatest sufferers of all, are kids.
cues.zh: 另一些受苦的人，也许是最受苦的，是孩子。

cues.en: Now this is unexpected because people move to the suburbs thinking that it's gonna be good for their kids.
cues.zh: 这挺出人意料的，因为人们搬到郊区时，以为这对孩子有好处。

cues.en: In fact, it is good for their kids to have a house and a lot. What's not good is that the kids can't get anywhere without being driven by parents.
cues.zh: 其实，孩子有房子和地块是好事。不好的地方在于，孩子没有父母开车送就哪儿也去不了。

cues.en: Everything they need. You give your kid an allowance, the kid has to beg to be driven somewhere to spend it.
cues.zh: 他们需要的一切。你给孩子零花钱，孩子还得求人开车送他去个地方才能花掉。

cues.en: The kids are delivered to the house at 03:00 in the afternoon by the school bus. If you don't want them warehoused in front of the television set, you need one or another of the parent needs to become a chauffeur.
cues.zh: 孩子们下午3点坐校车被送到家里。如果你不想把他们圈在电视机前，就得有父母中的一个人当司机。

cues.en: That has been the case with my sister in Miami. She was a journalist.
cues.zh: 我迈阿密的姐姐就是这样。她曾是记者。

cues.en: She had two children. For the last eight years, she has been a chauffeur. That has been her profession.
cues.zh: 她有两个孩子。过去八年，她一直当司机。这就是她的职业。

cues.en: On weekends, they call parents. Parents call each other to arrange for baseball games, and they have to put up with watching the baseball game for two hours so they can drive the kid back and so forth. Whatever happened to the system of the kid walking down
cues.zh: 到了周末，他们打电话叫家长。家长们互相打电话安排棒球比赛，还得忍着看两个小时的球，好开车把孩子接回来，诸如此类。以前那种孩子自己走着

cues.en: to the school and just, you know, picking up a bat and playing baseball? The kids are completely incapacitated
cues.zh: 去学校，你知道，随手拿起球棒就打棒球的方式，怎么就没了呢？在郊区的环境里，孩子们完全丧失了

cues.en: as independent beings in suburban conditions.
cues.zh: 作为独立个体的能力。

cues.en: Many people grew up in neighborhoods like this, where kids in neighborhoods... There's still a great memory in The United States of that. And they come up to me after the lectures and they confirm that it was wonderful when in fact they could get to school, they could get to the corner store, they could get to the movies. That is quickly disappearing.
cues.zh: 很多人就是在这样的社区长大的，那里的孩子们……美国至今仍对那种生活保有美好记忆。他们听完讲座后来找我，证实那种生活很棒——那时他们能自己去学校、去街角小店、去电影院。但这一切正在迅速消失。

cues.en: And there are kids that were actually, that led two lives, that grew up in a neighborhood and then at 13 or 14, they were taken out to the suburbs.
cues.zh: 还有些孩子其实过着两种生活：在社区里长大，然后到十三四岁时，被带到了郊区。

cues.en: And they come to me and say, now I understand why I became an unhappy person at 14. It wasn't puberty. It was the inability to actually have any have any freedom. Why is it?
cues.zh: 他们来找我说，我现在明白了，为什么我14岁时成了一个不快乐的人。不是青春期。而是根本没法拥有任何自由。为什么会这样？

cues.en: Why is it? You know, this is not a concentration camp here. This is a school. This is a school in Orlando. We're currently providing schools
cues.zh: 为什么会这样？你知道，这里不是集中营。这是一所学校。这是奥兰多的一所学校。我们目前提供的学校

cues.en: that are wooden barracks
cues.zh: 是木板搭的营房

cues.en: with air conditioning backpacks and chain link fences. This is a normative school now in the very wealthy state of Florida.
cues.zh: 配有空调、背包和铁丝网围栏。这就是如今在非常富裕的佛罗里达州的一所标准学校。

cues.en: How have we reached this situation
cues.zh: 我们怎么会走到这一步

cues.en: in which now, in our wealthiest years, we build public buildings that look like this, when in the thirties and forties and the eighteen nineties and the eighteen seventies and the eighteen sixties and the eighteen tens, we used to build magnificent public buildings
cues.zh: 如今，在我们最富有的年代，我们建的公共建筑却是这个样子；而在上世纪三十、四十年代，以及1890年代、1870年代、1860年代和1810年代，我们曾建造宏伟的公共建筑

cues.en: for our kids and for ourselves.
cues.zh: 为我们的孩子，也为我们自己。

cues.en: What we have done is we have reallotted the budget that we have, the public purse that is spent on infrastructure
cues.zh: 我们所做的是重新分配手中的预算，也就是用于基础设施的公共资金

cues.en: away from vertical infrastructure
cues.zh: 从垂直基础设施

cues.en: that people can use towards horizontal infrastructure that only cars can use. It's not that we're poorer.
cues.zh: 也就是人们能用的，转向只有汽车能用的水平基础设施。并不是我们变穷了。

cues.en: It's just that we're building gold plated highways. Nothing but the best for our cars.
cues.zh: 只是我们在修建镀金的高速公路。给我们的车用最好的，仅此而已。

cues.en: Every year, the standards get more generous for the cars. The lanes get wider.
cues.zh: 每年，针对汽车的标准都变得更宽松。车道也变得更宽。

cues.en: The centerline radii get get get get get get
cues.zh: 中心线半径 get get get get get get

cues.en: more, more generous and so forth. While for the schools, we become progressively accustomed to nothing but the worst for our kids. That is... That must be affecting society in a serious way. We can't afford day care centers, but we have we have budgets of billions for highways.
cues.zh: 更慷慨，诸如此类。而对于学校，我们却逐渐习惯了给孩子最差的东西。这……这肯定在严重地影响社会。我们负担不起日托中心，却有着……却有着数十亿美元的高速公路预算。

cues.en: Right now, this country, president Bush has committed us to additional billions for highways.
cues.zh: 眼下，这个国家，布什总统已经承诺为高速公路追加数十亿美元。

cues.en: There are states like Florida where the highway department budget approaches or exceeds the education department budget despite the absolute futility of building highways.
cues.zh: 有些州像佛罗里达，公路部门的预算接近甚至超过教育部门预算，尽管修建高速公路完全徒劳。

cues.en: Because as I've said earlier, very early on in the talk, it doesn't solve the traffic problem. In fact, let me quote a report from Los Angeles.
cues.zh: 因为正如我前面说过的，在演讲很早就说过，它解决不了交通问题。事实上，让我引用一份来自洛杉矶的报告。

cues.en: The Southern California Association of Governments,
cues.zh: 南加州政府协会，

cues.en: Los Angeles and its attendant communities,
cues.zh: 洛杉矶及其周边社区，

cues.en: completed a computer model of the year 2015
cues.zh: 完成了一个针对2015年的计算机模型，

cues.en: in which they modeled every possible alternative for traffic, including double decking highways,
cues.zh: 在模型中模拟了所有可能的交通替代方案，包括高速公路双层化、

cues.en: buying additional right of way, mandatory staggering of work hours,
cues.zh: 购买额外路权、强制错峰上下班、

cues.en: subsidizing of public transit.
cues.zh: 补贴公共交通。

cues.en: Their conclusion was,
cues.zh: 他们的结论是，

cues.en: nothing that can feasibly be done will have any but a cosmetic effect on the problem except for mixed use planning.
cues.zh: 除了混合用途规划外，任何可行措施对该问题都只会产生表面效果。

cues.en: Cosmetic being,
cues.zh: 表面性的存在，

cues.en: it... That's only a temporary solution.
cues.zh: 它……那只是临时方案。

cues.en: So all... Any and all money spent on building highways, as opposed to roads and streets, which are necessary, but on building highways,
cues.zh: 所以所有……任何花在修建高速公路上的钱，而不是花在道路和街道上——道路和街道是必要的——而是花在修建高速公路上，

cues.en: is absolutely
cues.zh: 绝对是

cues.en: down the barrel. Now for many years, we were able to afford that. We were able to afford the illusion that we could do that and also do this, but that's no longer the case. And you should fight this with all the energy that you have because it's really wasting,
cues.zh: 打了水漂。多年来，我们还能负担得起。我们还能负担得起这种幻觉：我们可以既做那件事，又做这件事，但情况已不再如此。你应该竭尽全力去抗争，因为它真的在浪费，

cues.en: your your treasure.
cues.zh: 你的，你的财富。

cues.en: One last individual,
cues.zh: 最后一个人，

cues.en: type of person that that suffers
cues.zh: 那种会遭受

cues.en: from,
cues.zh: ……之苦，

cues.en: this says from from before dawn to after dark, traffic governs Prince William family. These people, if you read this, actually don't have eight hour workdays. They have eleven hour workdays.
cues.zh: 这里说，从黎明前到天黑后，交通支配着 Prince William 一家。这些人，如果你读到这里，实际上并不是八小时工作制。他们是十一小时工作制。

cues.en: Because of the... When you factor in the commuting, we're right back to the standards
cues.zh: 因为……一旦把通勤算进去，我们就又回到了

cues.en: before of the industrial revolution.
cues.zh: 工业革命之前的标准。

cues.en: See, we think we work eight hours, but we have to commit one hour on either side,
cues.zh: 你看，我们以为自己工作八小时，但两头都得各花一小时，

cues.en: to something that is actually much more stressful than even the work usually, which is the commute.
cues.zh: 投入到通常比工作本身压力还大的事情上，也就是通勤。

cues.en: What the middle class does...
cues.zh: 中产阶级所做的……

cues.en: And the middle class in suburban sprawl is accustomed, is perfectly accustomed to commuting an hour to work and and and an hour back. What the middle class does
cues.zh: 而住在郊区扩张地带的中产阶级已经习惯，完全习惯了通勤一小时上班、再再再花一小时回家。中产阶级所做的

cues.en: by
cues.zh: 就是通过

cues.en: by spending those extra hours
cues.zh: 花掉这些额外的时间

cues.en: is that their quality of life drops drastically.
cues.zh: 使他们的生活质量急剧下降。

cues.en: Not their standard of living. The standard of living, in terms of square footage and washing machines, is perfect.
cues.zh: 不是他们的生活水平。就房屋面积和洗衣机而言，生活水平无可挑剔。

cues.en: The quality of life is very low.
cues.zh: 生活质量却非常低。

cues.en: Because if you commute one hour a day to work and one hour back, you're spending eight weeks in the car.
cues.zh: 因为如果你每天上班通勤一小时、下班再一小时，你就有八周时间待在车里。

cues.en: So you can add those eight weeks to your two week vacation, and you can see what that does to your quality of life. It's devastating.
cues.zh: 所以你可以把这八周加到两周假期上，看看它会怎样影响你的生活质量。结果是毁灭性的。

cues.en: You can also calculate the quality of life of your children.
cues.zh: 你也可以算算你孩子的生活质量。

cues.en: If you commute one hour a day over and back,
cues.zh: 如果你每天通勤往返共一小时，

cues.en: by the time your child is 18,
cues.zh: 到你孩子18岁时，

cues.en: you will have spent three years in the car.
cues.zh: 你会在车里度过三年。

cues.en: Three years of high quality time with your children, not at night, but good daytime hours that are... Cannot be spent with your kids. It's absolutely astonishing.
cues.zh: 三年高质量陪伴孩子的时间，不是在晚上，而是在白天那些……没法用来陪孩子的好时段。简直难以置信。

cues.en: And you can add to that the quality of life of the poor. Do you know that owning a car in The United States
cues.zh: 再加上穷人的生活质量。你知道在美国拥有一辆车

cues.en: costs $5,000
cues.zh: 要花 5,000 美元

cues.en: a year?
cues.zh: 一年？

cues.en: That $5,000
a year can sustain a $50,000
cues.zh: 一年能支撑 50,000 美元的

cues.en: mortgage.
cues.zh: 房贷。

cues.en: There is nothing that you can do in terms of making housing cheaper that can make a bigger dent in affordable housing than permitting a family to own one car less. In other words, to own just one car instead of two or two instead of three because that's $50,000.
cues.zh: 在让住房更便宜这件事上，没有什么比你允许一个家庭少拥有一辆车更能改善住房可负担性。换句话说，只拥有一辆车而不是两辆，或者两辆而不是三辆，因为那就是 50,000 美元。

cues.en: And that isn't a theoretical number.
cues.zh: 而且这不是理论上的数字。

cues.en: It's what the bankers call a back ratio.
cues.zh: 这就是银行家所说的“后比率”。

cues.en: See, when you apply for a mortgage loan, the front ratio is the the amount you're asking for relative to your income. The back ratio is the amount that you're asking for relative to all your debts.
cues.zh: 你看，申请房贷时，前比率是贷款额与收入之比；后比率是贷款额与全部债务之比。

cues.en: And bankers in in... For example, in Florida have told me that they often have to require people to sell cars before they qualify for mortgages because they can't... And what people do is in in fact, they sell the car, then they go right around and buy it back again after they qualify.
cues.zh: 比如佛罗里达的银行家告诉我，他们常常不得不要求人们在获得房贷资格前先卖掉车，因为他们没法……而人们实际上会怎么做呢：先把车卖掉，等符合资格后立刻又买回来。

cues.en: But the bankers aren't wrong.
cues.zh: 但银行家们并没有错。

cues.en: Those people, in fact, cannot afford the cars, and they're up to here in debt, with an... Holding two jobs, husband and wife working, weekends being busy. It's it's the most fantastically
cues.zh: 事实上，那些人根本买不起车，而且债台高筑，还……打着两份工，夫妻俩都上班，周末也忙个不停。这简直是最难以想象的

cues.en: low quality of life that you can imagine to be in the lower middle class in the suburb. It is much worse than any Italian with one third the income might experience.
cues.zh: 低质量生活，就是你能想象到的郊区中下阶层的生活。这比任何收入只有三分之一的意大利人所经历的都要糟糕得多。

cues.en: We're... I don't think, really, that as a people, we deserve this rotten deal that is being presented as as the American dream.
cues.zh: 我们……我真的不认为，作为一个民族，我们该承受这种被包装成美国梦的烂交易。

cues.en: And it is being every every
cues.zh: 而它正被每一个、每一个

cues.en: all the illusions that the marketing people, that the developers,
cues.zh: 所有那些营销人员、开发者制造的幻象，

cues.en: the television,
cues.zh: 电视，

cues.en: everything is actually selling this to to to the American citizen,
cues.zh: 这一切其实都是在向美国公民兜售这些，

cues.en: and very few people are providing the alternative. But the instant the alternative is provided and understood, they flock to it. In fact, the problem we have with all of our towns, the ones that are being built, is that even the small units become unaffordable
cues.zh: 而很少有人提供另一种选择。但一旦这种替代方案被提供并被理解，人们就会蜂拥而至。事实上，我们所有城镇、那些正在建设的城镇的问题在于，连小户型都变得难以负担

cues.en: because there's such there's such a a desirability to live in this kind of community. The experience of of Florida
cues.zh: 因为住在这样的社区里实在太有吸引力了。佛罗里达的体验

cues.en: and the prospect of planning in Florida is really quite depressing.
cues.zh: 而佛罗里达的规划前景实在令人沮丧。

cues.en: We're beginning now to enter a cycle of planning in which if everything goes very well,
cues.zh: 我们现在开始进入一个规划周期：如果一切顺利，

cues.en: an entire generation of planners will have the capability of spending billions of dollars. And in the end, what we will look back upon in the year 2010
cues.zh: 整整一代规划师都将有能力支出数十亿美元。而到最后，到2010年我们回顾时，

cues.en: is that the driving time has been restrained to forty minutes or to thirty minutes. That's all. That is really what's in the books now. That's what concurrency...
cues.zh: 会发现行车时间已被限制在四十分钟或三十分钟。就这样。这就是目前计划中的全部内容。这就是并发……

cues.en: The only thing that concurrency is worrying about is traffic driving time.
cues.zh: 并发唯一操心的是交通行驶时间。

cues.en: That is really unworthy
cues.zh: 那实在配不上

cues.en: of our capabilities and of our energies and of our political will. What we should be worrying about is the risk... The the restoring of communities like this. Everything that is in this photograph, in this old photograph, the types and quality of buildings, how they're assembled,
cues.zh: 我们的能力、精力和政治意愿。我们真正该担心的是风险……恢复像这样的社区。这张照片、这张老照片里的一切，建筑的类型和质量、它们如何组合，

cues.en: the street and what it's like, the the gathering of people of different ages and different incomes, the fantastic
cues.zh: 街道和它的样子，不同年龄、不同收入的人聚在一起，那种绝妙的

cues.en: the fantastic feeling of community, which is evident here. This is the human habitat. This is what we should, in fact, be instituting
cues.zh: 绝妙的社区感，在这里显而易见。这是人类的栖息地。这其实正是我们应该确立的

cues.en: in our codes and be worrying about in our planning.
cues.zh: 写进我们的规范，并在规划中操心的事。

cues.en: There is a great deal of distraction going on now towards
cues.zh: 现在有大量注意力正被分散到

cues.en: traffic movement and the ecological movement. A lot of energy is being spent in the in the safeguarding of weight... Of wet... Of wetlands,
cues.zh: 交通运动和生态运动上。大量精力被花在保护……湿……湿地上，

cues.en: which is a wonderful thing to do and very useful, but the same energy should be applied in the safeguarding of the human habitat. And that's really what I've been talking about today. Now I have simplified things somewhat. I can speak easily for another hour more talking about
cues.zh: 这是件好事，也非常有用，但同样的精力也应该用在保护人类栖息地上。这正是我今天一直在谈的。现在我多少简化了一下。我可以再轻松讲上一个小时，谈

cues.en: the technicalities of traffic and how they go through neighborhoods and so forth, but very few people can stand that much, in one, especially after lunch. Because this, in the end, is quite a depressing analysis, isn't it?
cues.zh: 交通的技术细节，以及交通如何穿过社区等等，但很少有人能一次承受这么多，尤其是在午饭后。因为归根结底，这是一项相当令人沮丧的分析，不是吗？
